Même si j'étais fatigué, je viendrais.
Si on télétravaillerait, on serait moins stressés.
Je ne sais pas s'il viendra.
Au cas où tu aurais faim, il y a du pain.
questions.explanation: Type 2 with si and with même si (avais / étais + conditionnel); si = whether takes the futur (viendra); au cas où takes the conditionnel (aurais). "Si on télétravaillerait" puts a conditionnel after si = if: it should be si on télétravaillait.

questions.stem: Name each numbered card on the "Changer de vie ?" board.

image.alt: A cork board titled Changer de vie ? with five numbered cards: 1, a price tag with three euro signs; 2, a laptop on a table next to a cup; 3, an alarm clock inside a circular arrow; 4, a person with a suitcase in front of a globe; 5, a signpost with two arrows pointing opposite ways.

questions.explanation: 1 le coût de la vie (prices: €€€), 2 le télétravail (a laptop at home), 3 la routine (the same day going round and round), 4 l'expatrié (someone with a suitcase who lives abroad), 5 le choix (two directions to choose from).

questions.stem: Which is the conditionnel passé of "venir" with "elle"?
questions.explanation: Venir takes être, in the conditionnel (serait), and the participle agrees with elle: venue. "Aurait venu" has the wrong auxiliary; "serait venu" lacks the agreement; "sera venue" is the futur antérieur.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu ___ me prévenir ! Je t'ai attendu une heure."
questions.explanation: A reproach about the past: tu aurais dû + infinitive (you should have). "Tu devrais" is advice about now or later; "tu as dû" means "you had to" or "you must have"; "aurais devoir" isn't a form.

questions.stem: What does "J'aurais pu venir." mean?
questions.explanation: J'aurais pu + infinitive = I could have (it was possible, but I didn't). "I should have come" is j'aurais dû venir; "I was able to come" is j'ai pu venir; "I could come" is je pourrais venir.

questions.stem: Which is the conditionnel passé of "se tromper" with "nous" (a group of men)?
questions.explanation: Pronominal verbs take être: nous nous serions trompés, with agreement. "Nous nous sommes trompés" is the passé composé.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ces photos ? Je les aurais ___ si j'avais su." (garder)
questions.explanation: With avoir, the participle agrees with a direct object placed before the verb: les = ces photos, feminine plural, so gardées.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a reproach to the person you are talking to?
questions.explanation: "Vous auriez pu appeler !" (you could have phoned) blames the listener. "J'aurais aimé être là" is a regret, "On aurait pu gagner" a missed possibility, and "L'incendie aurait fait deux blessés" is a news report of an unconfirmed fact.

questions.stem: In a news report: "Le voleur serait entré par la fenêtre." What does it mean?
choices: The thief would have got in through the window.
The thief should have got in through the window.
The thief will get in through the window.
The thief apparently got in through the window.
questions.explanation: In the news, the conditionnel passé reports an unconfirmed fact: "reportedly, apparently". It doesn't mean "would have" here.

questions.stem: You arrive at the station too late. How do you say "We should have left earlier" with "il faut"?
choices: Il faut être parti plus tôt.
Il aurait fallu partir plus tôt.
Il a fallu partir plus tôt.
questions.explanation: Il aurait fallu + infinitive = it would have been necessary (we should have). "Il faudrait" is about now or later, and "il a fallu" states a past fact (we had to).

questions.stem: What does "Il faut assumer ses choix." mean?
choices: You have to accept the consequences of your choices.
You have to assume your choices are right.
You have to make your choices quickly.
You have to change your choices.
questions.explanation: Assumer is a false friend: it means to accept responsibility for something. "To assume" in the sense of "suppose" is supposer.

questions.stem: Which word is an informal word for a social blunder, saying the wrong thing?
questions.explanation: Faire une gaffe = to put your foot in it. La honte is the shame you feel afterwards, le destin is fate, and une remarque is any remark.

questions.stem: Read: "À dix-huit ans, j'ai renoncé à partir en Australie. Aujourd'hui, je me dis que j'aurais dû partir." What does the writer feel?
choices: She went to Australia at eighteen.
She plans to go next year.
questions.explanation: J'ai renoncé à partir = I gave up on going; j'aurais dû partir = I should have gone. That is a regret.

questions.stem: Complete with "renoncer" in the present: "Si c'est trop cher, nous ___ au voyage."
questions.explanation: Before o, c becomes ç to keep the s sound: nous renonçons. Without the cedilla, "renoncons" would be said with a k sound.

questions.stem: Which is the conditionnel passé of "partir" for "je" (a man speaking)?
questions.explanation: Partir takes être: je serais parti. "J'aurais parti" uses the wrong auxiliary, "serais partir" uses the infinitive, and "j'aurai" is the futur.

questions.stem: Type the missing auxiliary: "J'___ aimé faire des études de médecine." (I would have liked)
questions.explanation: Aimer takes avoir; its conditionnel with je is aurais: j'aurais aimé. (J'aurai, without s, is the futur: "I will have".)

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "You shouldn't have said that."
questions.explanation: "Tu n'aurais pas dû dire ça." Ne … pas goes around the auxiliary (n'aurais pas), then dû, then the plain infinitive dire.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Devrais = should (now); aurais dû = should have; ai dû = had to; aurais pu = could have. "I can leave" would be je peux partir.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the conditionnel passé correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Il aurait fallu réserver plus tôt.
Ils auraient allés à la plage.
J'aurais voulu savoir si la chambre était libre.
questions.explanation: Aller takes être: ils seraient allés. The other four are correct: a missed possibility, a reproach, a past necessity and a polite request.

questions.stem: Name what each numbered panel shows.

image.alt: Five numbered panels: 1, a man with his arms up while a plate falls and lies broken on the floor; 2, three people at a table, the woman in the middle with red cheeks and a hand at her mouth, the others staring; 3, a man with red cheeks and his hands at his face; 4, a person pointing an accusing finger at another person, a clock above them; 5, a person with a question mark over the head in front of a signpost with two arrows.

questions.explanation: 1 la maladresse (a clumsy act: the plate), 2 la gaffe (she has just said the wrong thing), 3 la honte (shame), 4 le reproche (blaming someone for being late), 5 le dilemme (two ways, and no idea which to take).

questions.stem: Complete: "Si j'___ su, je serais venu."
questions.explanation: Type 3: si + plus-que-parfait (j'avais su), then the conditionnel passé (je serais venu). Never a conditionnel (aurais) after si.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si tu m'avais appelé, je t'___ aidé."
questions.explanation: After si + plus-que-parfait, the result about the past is in the conditionnel passé: je t'aurais aidé.

questions.stem: In standard French, complete: "Si j'avais pris le train, ___ déjà à Lyon maintenant."
questions.explanation: A past cause (si + plus-que-parfait) with a present result (maintenant): conditionnel présent, je serais. "Je serai" is a futur, and "j'étais / j'avais été" are not result forms in standard French.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si Marc parlait allemand, il ___ ce poste à Berlin l'année dernière."
questions.explanation: A lasting situation (he doesn't speak German: imparfait) with a past result (l'année dernière): conditionnel passé, il aurait accepté. "Accepterait" would put the result now.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Si j'avais su, je ne serai pas venu.
Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
Si j'aurais su, je ne serais pas venu.
Si j'avais su, je ne suis pas venu.
questions.explanation: Plus-que-parfait after si, conditionnel passé in the result: serais venu. "Si j'aurais su" is the classic mistake; "suis venu" and "serai venu" are not conditionnel forms.

questions.stem: What does "Si seulement je l'avais écouté !" express?
questions.explanation: Si seulement + plus-que-parfait = if only I had …: a regret. With the imparfait (si seulement j'avais le temps) it is a wish about now.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Si tu ne m'avais pas aidé, j'aurais abandonné."?
questions.explanation: Sans + noun replaces the si clause and keeps the conditionnel passé. The futur (abandonnerai) and the passé composé (ai abandonné) would state something real.

questions.stem: Facts: "Il pleuvait, alors nous ne sommes pas sortis." Which sentence imagines the past differently?
choices: S'il ne pleut pas, nous sortirons.
S'il avait plu, nous serions sortis.
S'il n'avait pas plu, nous serions sortis.
S'il n'avait pas plu, nous ne serions pas sortis.
questions.explanation: Reverse both facts: it rained → if it hadn't rained; we didn't go out → we would have gone out. "S'il ne pleut pas, nous sortirons" is a type-1 plan, not the past; the other two keep one of the facts unchanged.

questions.stem: What does "J'ai eu le coup de foudre pour Lisbonne." mean?
choices: I had a stroke of luck in Lisbon.
I was struck by lightning in Lisbon.
I had a terrible time in Lisbon.
I fell in love with Lisbon at first sight.
questions.explanation: Le coup de foudre (literally a lightning strike) is love at first sight, for a person or a place. A stroke of luck is un coup de chance.

questions.stem: Which verb means "to retrain, to change careers"?
questions.explanation: Se reconvertir (la reconversion). Se débrouiller = to get by, s'en sortir = to pull through, se décider = to make up your mind.

questions.stem: What does "Je me débrouille en espagnol." mean?
choices: I don't speak a word of Spanish.
questions.explanation: Se débrouiller = to manage, to get by: enough to cope, not fluent.

questions.stem: Read: "Si ma voiture n'était pas tombée en panne ce soir-là, je serais encore à la banque." What do we learn?
choices: Her car broke down, and she no longer works at the bank.
Her car didn't break down, and she still works at the bank.
She will leave the bank if her car breaks down.
Her car broke down, and she still works at the bank.
questions.explanation: Reverse the unreal sentence to get the facts: the car did break down (that evening), and today she is not at the bank any more (serais encore = would still be).

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "croiser" correctly?
choices: Je croise que tu as raison.
J'ai croisé la rue au feu rouge.
Nous avons croisé à la gare.
J'ai croisé Paul à la boulangerie ce matin.
questions.explanation: Croiser quelqu'un = to come across or pass someone. To cross a street is traverser; "je croise que" means nothing; croiser needs an object (nous nous sommes croisés à la gare).

questions.stem: Type the plus-que-parfait of "partir" (a group of friends, "nous"): "Si nous ___ ___ plus tôt, nous n'aurions pas raté le train."
questions.explanation: Partir takes être, and the participle agrees with nous: si nous étions partis (or parties for an all-female group) plus tôt.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If only I had known!"
questions.explanation: "Si seulement j'avais su !" Si seulement + plus-que-parfait: a regret, with no main clause.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the times of its two halves.
left: Si j'avais su, je serais venu.
Si j'avais pris le train, je serais déjà là.
Si j'étais plus courageux, je l'aurais fait.
Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais.
questions.explanation: Plus-que-parfait + conditionnel passé: past/past (type 3). Plus-que-parfait + conditionnel présent: past/now. Imparfait + conditionnel passé: always/past. Imparfait + conditionnel présent: now/now (type 2).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Si elle était partie à l'heure, elle serait arrivée à temps.
Si on s'était couchés plus tôt, on serait moins fatigués.
Si tu aurais demandé, je t'aurais aidé.
Si seulement il avait eu plus de chance !
questions.explanation: Only "si tu aurais demandé" is wrong: no conditionnel after si (si tu avais demandé). The others are type 3, a mixed conditional, à ta place + conditionnel passé, and si seulement + plus-que-parfait.

questions.stem: Name the tense in each numbered box.

image.alt: Two rows. Top: a box marked past, Si j'avais pris le train, with empty box 1, and an arrow to a box marked now, je serais déjà là, with empty box 2. Bottom: a box marked always, Si j'étais plus courageux, with empty box 3, and an arrow to a box marked past, je l'aurais fait, with empty box 4. A timeline is under each row.

questions.explanation: 1 j'avais pris: plus-que-parfait; 2 je serais: conditionnel présent (a result now); 3 j'étais: imparfait (a lasting trait); 4 j'aurais fait: conditionnel passé (a past result).

questions.stem: In written French, complete: "Quand tu ___ à Paris, appelle-moi."
questions.explanation: After quand, a future action takes the futur: quand tu arriveras (English: when you arrive). The conditionnel and the imparfait don't fit a future plan.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Dès que j'___ la réponse, je vous écrirai." (the answer must have arrived first)
questions.explanation: The action finished before another future one takes the futur antérieur: j'aurai reçu (futur of avoir, no s). "Aurais reçu" is the conditionnel passé.

questions.stem: Which is the futur antérieur of "partir" with "elles"?
questions.explanation: Partir takes être, in the futur (seront), with agreement: parties. "Seraient parties" is the conditionnel passé.

questions.stem: Complete: "D'ici 2030, la ville ___ trois nouvelles lignes de tram."
questions.explanation: D'ici + a future date: what will be finished by then, futur antérieur (aura construit). The passé composé and the imparfait are past tenses; aurait construit is the conditionnel passé.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Quand tu viendras, on ira au cinéma.
Quand tu viendrais, on ira au cinéma.
Si tu viendrais, on ira au cinéma.
Si tu viendras, on ira au cinéma.
questions.explanation: Quand + futur for a future event. Si = if never takes the futur or the conditionnel: si tu viens, on ira au cinéma.

questions.stem: "Paul n'est pas là ? Il aura oublié." What does "il aura oublié" mean here?
questions.explanation: The futur antérieur can make a guess about the past: il aura oublié = he must have forgotten (= il a dû oublier).

questions.stem: Which sentence describes a habit, not a future plan?
choices: S'il pleut demain, je prendrai le bus.
Quand il pleut, je prends le bus.
Quand il aura plu, je prendrai le bus.
Quand il pleuvra, je prendrai le bus.
questions.explanation: Quand + present, then present: whenever it rains (a habit). The others are about the future: quand + futur, quand + futur antérieur, and a type-1 si-clause about tomorrow.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tant que les travaux ___, la rue restera fermée."
questions.explanation: Tant que (as long as) + futur for a future situation: tant que les travaux dureront. The other forms are past or conditionnel.

questions.stem: What is "le chantier"?
questions.explanation: Le chantier is the building site (la rue est en chantier). A scale model is une maquette, a cycle lane une piste cyclable.

questions.stem: Which word is the scale model that architects show before a building is built?
questions.explanation: La maquette. La prévision is a forecast, la zone an area, l'urbanisme town planning.

questions.stem: Read: "Dès que l'école aura fermé pour les vacances, les ouvriers commenceront sa rénovation." What happens first?
choices: The school closes for the holidays.
questions.explanation: The futur antérieur (aura fermé) marks what happens first; the futur simple (commenceront) what follows.

questions.stem: What does "La mairie va aménager les bords de la rivière." mean?
choices: The town hall is going to move to the riverbanks.
The town hall is going to clean the river.
The town hall is going to develop the riverbanks.
The town hall is going to sell the riverbanks.
questions.explanation: Aménager = to develop or lay out an area. Moving house is déménager.

questions.stem: Complete with "financer" in the present: "Nous ___ la moitié du projet."
questions.explanation: Like renoncer: c becomes ç before o, nous finançons. The e (financeons) is the trick for -ger verbs, not -cer verbs.

questions.stem: Type the missing auxiliary: "Quand tu ___ fini, tu m'appelleras."
questions.explanation: Futur antérieur: the futur of avoir (tu auras) + fini. First you finish, then you call.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "By tomorrow, I will have finished the report."
questions.explanation: "D'ici demain, j'aurai terminé le rapport." D'ici + time, then the futur antérieur (j'aurai terminé).

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its tense.
questions.explanation: Aller + infinitive: futur proche. Stem + -ai: futur simple. Aurai + participle: futur antérieur. Aurais + participle: conditionnel passé (one letter more).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Une fois que tu seras installé, tu m'inviteras.
Quand j'aurais reçu ton message, je te répondrai.
Quand je serai arrivée, je t'enverrai un message.
Si tu viendras, je serai content.
questions.explanation: "Quand j'aurais reçu" uses the conditionnel passé after quand (it should be j'aurai reçu), and "si tu viendras" puts a futur after si (si tu viens). The other three use the futur or futur antérieur correctly; the main clause can be an imperative.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the town plan.

image.alt: A town plan in two halves, Aujourd'hui and En 2030. 1, a fenced building site with a crane, on the left. On the right: 2, a tram on rails; 3, a green lane with a bicycle symbol; 4, a paved square with people walking and a no-cars sign.

questions.explanation: 1 le chantier (the building site with its crane), 2 le tramway, 3 la piste cyclable (the bicycle symbol), 4 la zone piétonne (people only, no cars). There is no roundabout, and the plan itself is not a model.

questions.stem: How is the word "uchronie" made?
choices: From the name of a French town.
From the name of a novel by Napoléon.
From an old word for a battle.
questions.explanation: A utopia is "no place"; an uchronie is "no time": a time that never existed. The word was coined by Charles Renouvier.

questions.stem: Which statement about the history of the genre matches the lesson?
choices: Renouvier coined "uchronie"; Geoffroy's Napoléon book (1836) came earlier.
The first uchronia was written after the Second World War.
questions.explanation: The word appeared in 1857 and Renouvier's book Uchronie in 1876; Louis Geoffroy's Napoléon et la conquête du monde (1812–1832) dates from 1836.

questions.stem: On which date was the Battle of Waterloo?
questions.explanation: 18 June 1815. Ligny was on 16 June, the second abdication on 22 June, and Napoléon was back in Paris on 20 March.

questions.stem: According to the fact text, why did the French attack at Waterloo begin late?
choices: Napoléon was waiting for Louis XVIII.
Grouchy had taken all the artillery.
Heavy rain the day before had soaked the ground.
The Prussians attacked first in the morning.
questions.explanation: Il a plu très fort la veille: le sol était trempé, so the attack only began towards the end of the morning.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si Grouchy ___ à temps, Napoléon aurait peut-être gagné."
questions.explanation: Type 3: si + plus-que-parfait. Arriver takes être: était arrivé. No conditionnel after si.

questions.stem: "Si Napoléon avait gagné, Waterloo serait le nom d'une victoire." What kind of sentence is this?
choices: a mixed conditional: past cause, present result
a type 3 si-clause: past cause, past result
questions.explanation: Plus-que-parfait after si (a past cause) and conditionnel présent in the result (today's situation): a mixed conditional.

questions.stem: Which sentence states a historical fact?
choices: Les Prussiens seraient arrivés trop tard.
Son fils aurait régné après lui.
questions.explanation: Facts stay in the indicative (a abdiqué). The three sentences in the conditionnel passé belong to the fiction.

questions.stem: You are writing an uchronia. Which is the most careful way to give an invented result?
choices: Napoléon aurait peut-être gagné la bataille.
questions.explanation: An invented past result: conditionnel passé, with a hedge (peut-être). The passé composé and the plus-que-parfait would state it as a fact; gagnerait puts it in the present.

questions.stem: Which is the correct present of "vaincre" with "il"?
questions.explanation: Il vainc, with no t; ils vainquent (c → qu before a vowel). In everyday French, battre is more common.

questions.stem: Type the missing noun (with no article): the opposite of "la victoire" is "la ___".
questions.explanation: La défaite (defeat). Don't confuse it with le défaut (a flaw).

questions.stem: Put these events of 1815 in the order they happened.
choices: Napoléon is back at the Tuileries in Paris
questions.explanation: 20 March (Tuileries), 16 June (Ligny), 18 June (Waterloo), 22 June (abdication), 15 October (Saint Helena).

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: L'empereur (feminine l'impératrice), le règne (from régner), la conquête, l'armée. A kingdom is un royaume, not taught here.

questions.stem: Which statements are facts given in the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: Napoléon abdicated in favour of his son.
Grouchy arrived at Waterloo in time.
Blücher's Prussians reached the battlefield in the afternoon.
Napoléon died on Saint Helena in 1821.
Wellington's army fled at the start of the battle.
questions.explanation: Fact: the abdication of 22 June in favour of his son, the Prussians' arrival in the afternoon, and his death on Saint Helena on 5 May 1821. Grouchy didn't arrive, and Wellington's army held out all day.

questions.stem: Continue the chain: "S'il avait attaqué dès le matin, les Prussiens ne seraient pas arrivés à temps. Si les Prussiens n'___ pas ___ à temps, Wellington se serait retiré." (arriver)
questions.explanation: The result of one sentence (ne seraient pas arrivés) becomes the next si clause in the plus-que-parfait: si les Prussiens n'étaient pas arrivés. The conditionnel never moves to the si side.

questions.stem: Choose the best translation of "Le suspect serait en fuite."
choices: The suspect would be on the run.
The suspect should be on the run.
The suspect is reportedly on the run.
The suspect will be on the run.
questions.explanation: The reportive conditional means "reportedly, is said to". It is not "would" here.

questions.stem: A news site writes: "L'accident aurait fait trois blessés." What is it telling you?
choices: Three people were reportedly injured; it isn't confirmed yet.
Three people may be injured in a future accident.
Three people would have been injured if the driver had been faster.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel passé in a news report passes on unconfirmed information about the past.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents the information as confirmed?
choices: Selon nos informations, le musée fermerait.
Le musée aurait fermé ses portes.
La mairie a confirmé la fermeture du musée.
questions.explanation: Only "La mairie a confirmé la fermeture du musée" is in the indicative with an official source. The others use the reportive conditional; vraisemblablement means "in all likelihood", which is still not confirmed.

questions.stem: What does "démentir" mean in "La mairie a démenti l'information."?
questions.explanation: Démentir is to deny a report officially (un démenti). Mentir is to lie.

questions.stem: Rewrite as an unconfirmed report: "Les suspects sont partis en voiture."
choices: Les suspects partiraient en voiture hier.
Les suspects étaient partis en voiture.
Les suspects auraient partis en voiture.
Les suspects seraient partis en voiture.
questions.explanation: Keep the auxiliary (être) and the agreement, and put the auxiliary in the conditionnel: seraient partis. "Étaient partis" is a plus-que-parfait, still a fact.

questions.stem: What does "Selon nos informations" tell the reader?
choices: The information has been officially confirmed.
The paper's own sources say it, but no official has confirmed it.
A news agency has denied it.
questions.explanation: Selon nos informations = according to our (the paper's) sources: nobody official has said it yet, which is why the verb that follows is usually in the conditionnel.

questions.stem: What is "un bilan provisoire"?
choices: a provisional toll that may still change
questions.explanation: Provisoire = provisional, temporary. The final figure may be different.

questions.stem: Which statement about the AFP matches the lesson?
choices: It is the ministry in charge of the press.
It is a French news agency founded under that name in 1944.
It wrote the Charter of Munich.
It is a daily newspaper founded in 1835.
questions.explanation: The Agence France-Presse took that name in 1944; it continued the Agence Havas, which dates from 1835.

questions.stem: In which sentence is the conditionnel NOT reportive?
choices: Le ministre démissionnerait demain, selon une source proche.
Si j'avais le temps, je lirais plus de journaux.
D'après des témoins, le feu aurait commencé vers minuit.
Selon la police, le voleur aurait agi seul.
questions.explanation: "Si j'avais le temps, je lirais …" is a type-2 si-clause (would). The other three report unconfirmed information, each with a source (selon, d'après).

questions.stem: Type the auxiliary for an unconfirmed report: "Selon la police, le voleur ___ quitté le pays."
questions.explanation: Quitter takes avoir; for an unconfirmed past fact, the auxiliary goes in the conditionnel: il aurait quitté.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a news story that turns out to be true in order.
choices: A first report in the conditionnel, with a source
questions.explanation: A claim is reported with the conditionnel and a source; once it is confirmed officially, the verbs switch to the indicative.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Présumé = alleged (l'auteur présumé), provisoire = provisional (un bilan provisoire), vraisemblablement = in all likelihood, de source sûre = from a reliable (but unnamed) source. Officially is officiellement.

questions.stem: Which are signals that information is not (yet) confirmed? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The reportive conditional, présumé, provisoire and vraisemblablement all signal caution. "La mairie a confirmé" is an official confirmation, in the indicative.

questions.stem: Read: "Selon les pompiers, il n'y a pas de victimes. D'après des témoins, le feu aurait commencé vers deux heures." Which piece of information is presented as unconfirmed?
questions.explanation: Aurait commencé is a reportive conditional, sourced to witnesses. "Il n'y a pas de victimes" is in the indicative, from the fire brigade.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le livre ___ j'ai besoin."
questions.explanation: Avoir besoin takes de (j'ai besoin de ce livre), so the relative is dont: le livre dont j'ai besoin. "Que" is for a direct object, "qui" for a subject and "où" for a place or time.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "the painter whose works I know"?
choices: le peintre dont les œuvres je connais
le peintre que je connais ses œuvres
le peintre dont je connais les œuvres
le peintre dont je connais ses œuvres
questions.explanation: After dont, French keeps the normal order (je connais les œuvres) and the article les. "Dont les œuvres je connais" copies English word order; "que … ses œuvres" and "dont … ses œuvres" say "his" twice, because dont already means "whose".

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce ___ m'intéresse, c'est l'art contemporain."
questions.explanation: The gap is the subject of intéresse (it interests me), so ce qui. Ce que is followed by a subject (ce que j'aime), ce dont by a verb with de, ce à quoi by a verb with à.

questions.stem: Complete in careful French: "___ j'ai besoin, c'est de calme."
questions.explanation: Avoir besoin de takes de, so "what I need" is ce dont j'ai besoin. Careful French repeats de after c'est: c'est de calme. Ce que would need a direct object verb (ce que je veux).

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce ___ je pense, c'est à nos vacances."
questions.explanation: Penser takes à (je pense à nos vacances), and with no noun the relative after à is quoi: ce à quoi je pense. The à after c'est confirms it.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est moi qui ___ choisi ce tableau."
questions.explanation: After c'est moi qui, the verb agrees with moi, so it's the je form: c'est moi qui ai choisi. "C'est moi qui a" is a common slip in speech, but it's wrong in writing.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les tableaux dont je t'ai ___ sont au premier étage."
questions.explanation: Dont is never a direct object, so the participle doesn't agree: les tableaux dont je t'ai parlé. (Compare les tableaux que j'ai vus, where que is a direct object.)

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est cette sculpture que j'ai ___."
questions.explanation: Que stands for cette sculpture (feminine), a direct object placed before avoir, so the participle agrees: achetée.

questions.stem: Which phrase is the usual way to say "the town the painter comes from"?
choices: la ville d'où vient le peintre
la ville dont vient le peintre
la ville où vient le peintre
la ville que vient le peintre
questions.explanation: For coming from a place, French uses d'où (venir de + a place). "La ville dont il vient" is old literary French, "où vient" means "where he is coming to", and que can't be used with venir de.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce tableau ne représente rien de réel : c'est de l'art ___."
questions.explanation: Art that doesn't show real things is abstrait (abstract). Classique and ancien are about the period or style, and "réel" contradicts the first half of the sentence.

questions.stem: What does "Ce portrait m'a beaucoup touchée" mean, said by a woman?
choices: I touched this portrait a lot.
This portrait moved me a lot.
This portrait annoyed me a lot.
I painted this portrait with care.
questions.explanation: Toucher means "to touch" and also "to move (emotionally)". With a painting as the subject, it's the second: it moved me. Touchée agrees with m' (a woman), a direct object before avoir.

questions.stem: Read: "Le musée dont je te parle a ouvert en 2020. Ce qui le rend unique, c'est sa collection de dessins d'enfants. Mais ce que je préfère, c'est la salle où on peut dessiner soi-même." What does the speaker like best?
choices: the fact that the museum is new
the room where you can draw yourself
questions.explanation: Ce que je préfère, c'est … = what I prefer is … : la salle où on peut dessiner soi-même. The collection is what makes the museum unique (ce qui le rend unique), not what the speaker prefers.

questions.stem: Which sentence puts "à Giverny" in the spotlight, in careful French?
choices: C'est à Giverny où Monet a peint ses nymphéas.
C'est à Giverny qui Monet a peint ses nymphéas.
C'est à Giverny que Monet a peint ses nymphéas.
C'est à Giverny dont Monet a peint ses nymphéas.
questions.explanation: In the c'est … que frame, anything that isn't the subject (here a place with à) is followed by que. "C'est à Giverny où …" (like "c'est là où …") is common in speech, but careful French uses que; qui would mean Giverny painted something, and dont needs de.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: Voici le dessin dont je suis fier.
C'est l'artiste dont le fils est sculpteur.
C'est le musée que je t'ai parlé.
C'est le peintre dont j'admire ses couleurs.
questions.explanation: Fier de → dont; dont le fils = whose son; ce que = what (object). "Le musée que je t'ai parlé" needs dont (parler de), and "dont j'admire ses couleurs" says "his" twice: dont j'admire les couleurs.

questions.stem: Complete with ce qui, ce que or ce dont: "___ j'ai envie, c'est d'un café."
questions.explanation: Avoir envie de takes de, so "what I want" is ce dont j'ai envie, and careful French repeats de after c'est (c'est d'un café).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "It's the painter whose works I love."
questions.explanation: C'est le peintre dont j'adore les œuvres. After dont the clause keeps its normal order, subject + verb + object (j'adore les œuvres), unlike English "whose works I love".

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the relative pronoun that fills the gap.
left: le film ___ tout le monde parle
questions.explanation: Je lis le livre: direct object → que. L'ami habite à Lyon: subject → qui. Je suis née dans cette ville: a place → où. Tout le monde parle de ce film: de + noun → dont.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things on this museum wall.

image.alt: A museum wall with four numbered things: a framed head-and-shoulders painting of a person on the left, a pencil drawing of a cat on paper, a large landscape painting in a gold frame behind a red rope, and a grey statue on a plinth on the right.

questions.explanation: 1 shows a person: le portrait. 2 is a pencil sketch on paper: le dessin. 3 is the famous painting protected by a rope: le chef-d'œuvre (plural les chefs-d'œuvre). 4 is a statue: la sculpture. Le peintre is a person, and le style isn't an object.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le projet sur ___ je travaille."
questions.explanation: After a preposition (sur), a thing takes the lequel family, agreeing with the antecedent: le projet (masculine singular) → lequel. Qui after a preposition is for people, and dont replaces de.

questions.stem: Complete: "Voilà la raison pour ___ il est parti."
questions.explanation: Raison is feminine, so pour laquelle. Quoi is only used when there's no noun (ce pour quoi), and qui after a preposition refers to people.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le salon ___ nous participons." (participer à)
questions.explanation: Participer takes à, and à + lequel contracts to auquel, like à + le → au. "À lequel" doesn't exist; duquel and dont contain de.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est la réunion au cours de ___ il a présenté le projet."
questions.explanation: Au cours de is a compound preposition, so the lequel family follows; réunion is feminine, and de + laquelle doesn't contract: au cours de laquelle. Dont is never used after a preposition.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le parc près ___ j'habite."
questions.explanation: Près de is a compound preposition; de + lequel contracts to duquel: le parc près duquel j'habite. Dont can't follow a preposition, "de lequel" must contract, and près où isn't French.

questions.stem: Complete: "La collègue avec ___ je travaille est très sympa."
questions.explanation: For a person after a preposition, use qui: avec qui (avec laquelle is also correct). Que can't follow a preposition, dont replaces de, and quoi is for things with no noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Voici les candidats parmi ___ nous avons choisi."
questions.explanation: After parmi (among) and entre, French uses the lequel family even for people: parmi lesquels (masculine plural). "Parmi qui" isn't used.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le projet ___ je suis responsable."
questions.explanation: Here de belongs to the adjective (responsable de), not to a compound preposition, so dont. Duquel is for compound prepositions such as près de or au cours de.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce sont des questions ___ je n'ai pas pu répondre." (répondre à)
questions.explanation: Répondre takes à; questions is feminine plural; à + lesquelles contracts to auxquelles. Auxquels is masculine, and desquelles contains de.

questions.stem: What does "Il travaille pour une société de conseil" mean?
choices: He works for a consultation service for society.
He works for a club that gives advice.
He works for a consulting firm.
questions.explanation: La société here is a company, a firm (it also means society in general). Une société de conseil is a consulting firm.

questions.stem: What is "le chiffre d'affaires" of a company?
choices: its turnover: the total amount it sells
questions.explanation: Le chiffre d'affaires is the turnover (revenue). Profit is le bénéfice, which is what is left after costs.

questions.stem: Read: "Le service dans lequel je travaille s'occupe des clients. Ma responsable, avec qui je m'entends très bien, dirige une équipe de huit personnes." Who runs the team of eight?
questions.explanation: Ma responsable … dirige une équipe de huit personnes: the manager runs the team. Avec qui je m'entends très bien (who I get on with very well) is a relative clause about her.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est la conférence à laquelle j'ai ___." (assister à = to attend)
questions.explanation: À laquelle is not a direct object, so the participle doesn't agree: j'ai assisté. Agreement with avoir only happens with a direct object before the verb (la conférence que j'ai organisée).

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: le bureau dans lequel je travaille
le bureau sur qui je travaille
le bureau à côté duquel je me gare
questions.explanation: Où and dans lequel are both fine for a place, and à côté duquel follows a compound preposition. Travailler doesn't take de, so dont is wrong, and qui after a preposition is for people, not a desk or an office.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "C'est un projet ___ je pense depuis longtemps." (penser à)
questions.explanation: Penser takes à; projet is masculine singular; à + lequel → auquel. (Ce à quoi is only for "what", when there's no noun.)

questions.stem: Put in order: "The meeting during which he presented the project was long."
questions.explanation: La réunion au cours de laquelle il a présenté le projet était longue. The relative clause comes straight after its antecedent (la réunion), and the preposition comes first, as in English "during which".

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the pronoun that fills the gap.
left: le bâtiment à côté ___ je travaille
questions.explanation: Participer à + masculine → auquel; assister à + feminine → à laquelle (no contraction); à côté de + masculine → duquel; sur + masculine plural → lesquels. Dont never follows a preposition.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this company chart.

image.alt: A company chart with six numbered parts: an office building at the top left, a box of three people at the top centre, three department boxes below it (commercial, technique, clients), one person at the top of the clients box, four people at the bottom of that box, and a lorry with boxes on the right with an arrow pointing to the company.

questions.explanation: 1 is the head office building, le siège. 2 is the group at the top that runs the company, la direction. 3 is a department, le service (technique). 4 is the person in charge of the clients department, la responsable. 5 is one of the employees, le salarié. 6 delivers goods to the company: le fournisseur (supplier). A concurrent would be a rival firm, and le chiffre d'affaires is a sum of money.

questions.stem: Complete in the passive (passé composé): "La maison ___ en 1990."
questions.explanation: Passé composé passive = a été + participle agreeing with the subject: la maison (feminine) → a été construite. "A construit" is active, "a été construit" lacks the agreement, and "est construit" is present and masculine.

questions.stem: Complete in the futur passive: "Ces voitures ___ en Espagne l'an prochain."
questions.explanation: The tense is carried by être: futur → seront. Voitures is feminine plural, so fabriquées. "Sont" is present, "ont été" passé composé, and "fabriqués" is masculine.

questions.stem: Make it passive: "On doit réparer le toit."
choices: Le toit est dû être réparé.
questions.explanation: With a modal verb, the passive is devoir + être + participle: doit être réparé. Être must stay in the infinitive after doit; "été" is a participle and can't follow doit.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses de correctly to introduce the agent?
choices: Le pont a été construit d'une entreprise lyonnaise.
La lettre a été écrite de ma sœur.
Le magasin a été cambriolé de deux hommes.
Ce chef est respecté de tous ses collègues.
questions.explanation: De introduces the agent after verbs of feeling and state (aimé, respecté, connu, entouré): respecté de tous. For real actions such as building, writing or burgling, the agent takes par: construit par une entreprise, écrite par ma sœur.

questions.stem: How do you say "I was given a book" in natural French?
questions.explanation: Donner quelque chose à quelqu'un: me is an indirect object, so it can't become the subject of a passive. French uses on: On m'a donné un livre. (Un livre m'a été donné is possible but formal.)

questions.stem: Complete: "Les lettres ont ___ envoyées hier."
questions.explanation: Été, the participle of être, never changes. It's the second participle, envoyées, that agrees with les lettres.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the passive?
choices: Elle est partie à huit heures.
La porte est fermée chaque soir par le gardien.
questions.explanation: A passive has a verb with a direct object (fermer la porte) and can take par + someone doing the action: fermée par le gardien. Partir and arriver are verbs that take être in the passé composé, and se lever is pronominal; none of them is a passive.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "White wine is drunk chilled" (as a general rule)?
choices: Le vin blanc se boit frais.
Le vin blanc se bois frais.
Le vin blanc s'est bu frais.
questions.explanation: The pronominal passive (se + verb in the third person) describes how something is usually done: se boit. "Boit" without se would mean the wine drinks; "se bois" is the je/tu form; "s'est bu" is past (was drunk).

questions.stem: Make it passive: "On fabriquait ces jouets à la main."
choices: Ces jouets étaient fabriqués à la main.
Ces jouets ont été fabriqués à la main.
Ces jouets sont fabriqués à la main.
Ces jouets avaient été fabriqués à la main.
questions.explanation: Être takes the tense of the active verb: fabriquait is imparfait → étaient. Jouets is masculine plural → fabriqués. The other choices change the tense.

questions.stem: On a jumper, what is "l'étiquette"?
choices: the price you pay at the till
the wool it is made of
the label with its origin and washing instructions
questions.explanation: L'étiquette is the label (or tag): Lisez l'étiquette avant de laver ce pull. It also means etiquette (good manners).

questions.stem: What does "des couteaux artisanaux" mean?
choices: knives made on a production line
knives made by craftspeople in small workshops
questions.explanation: Artisanal (plural artisanaux) means made by an artisan, a craftsperson, usually by hand in a small workshop. Industriel would describe factory production.

questions.stem: Read: "En 2015, un site internet a été créé, et aujourd'hui un tiers des couteaux sont exportés." What happens to a third of the knives?
choices: They are sold only on the website.
questions.explanation: Exporter = to sell to other countries: un tiers des couteaux sont exportés = a third of the knives are exported. The website was created in 2015, but the text doesn't say the knives are only sold there.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les billets ___ en une heure." (They sold out in an hour.)
questions.explanation: A pronominal passive in the passé composé takes être and agrees with the subject: les billets (masculine plural) → se sont vendus. "Vendues" is feminine; "ont été vendu" lacks the agreement.

questions.stem: Which passive sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: La tour a été terminée en 1889.
Les usines ont été fermées en 2010.
La porte a été ouvert par le gardien.
Le pont sera construit par une entreprise belge.
questions.explanation: Terminée and fermées agree with their feminine subjects, and sera construit is a correct futur passive. "La porte a été ouvert" lacks the agreement (ouverte), and été never agrees ("étées" doesn't exist).

questions.stem: Put the verb in the passive, passé composé: "Cette robe ___ (fabriquer) au Maroc."
questions.explanation: Passé composé of être (a été) + the participle agreeing with robe (feminine singular): a été fabriquée.

questions.stem: Put in order: "The new machines were installed by the manufacturer."
questions.explanation: Les nouvelles machines ont été installées par le fabricant. Auxiliary (ont), then été, then the participle agreeing with machines (installées), then the agent with par.

questions.stem: Match each active sentence to its passive.
left: On vendra les billets en ligne.
On vendait ces voitures en Italie.
choices: Les billets seront vendus en ligne.
Ces voitures étaient vendues en Italie.
Les billets ont été vendus en ligne.
questions.explanation: Être takes the tense of the active verb: vend → est vendu, a vendu → a été vendue, vendra → seront vendus, vendait → étaient vendues. The participle agrees with the new subject. The distractors have a missing agreement or the wrong tense.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this factory scene.

image.alt: A cutaway factory with five numbered parts: the building with its saw-tooth roof, a pile of logs on the left, a machine with a cutting wheel, a conveyor belt carrying wooden chairs, and a white label on a cardboard box on the right.

questions.explanation: 1 is the whole building: l'usine. 2 is the wood the chairs are made from: la matière première. 3 cuts the wood: la machine. 4 carries the products along: la chaîne (production line). 5 is the label on the box: l'étiquette. No consumer is shown, and la qualité isn't an object.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu me prêtes ton vélo ? — Oui, je ___ prête."
questions.explanation: Columns 1 then 2: te (to you) before le (it): je te le prête. Lui is "to him / her", not "to you".

questions.stem: Replace both objects: "J'ai rendu les clés à Inès." → "Je ___ ai rendues."
questions.explanation: Les (the keys, column 2) comes before lui (to her, column 3): je les lui ai rendues. Leur is plural (to them). Rendues agrees with les (les clés).

questions.stem: Complete: "Il reste du pain ? — Oui, il ___ a."
questions.explanation: Il y a + en (some): y comes before en, so il y en a. En is always last.

questions.stem: How do you say "Give it to me!" (the book) in standard French?
questions.explanation: In an affirmative command the direct object comes first and me becomes moi: donne-le-moi. "Donne-moi-le" is heard in casual speech but isn't standard; "me le donne" is statement order, and "me" can't end a command.

questions.stem: How do you say "Give me some!" (vous) in standard French?
questions.explanation: En is always last, and moi becomes m' before en: donnez-m'en.

questions.stem: How do you say "Don't tell him (it)!"?
questions.explanation: Negative commands keep the normal statement order before the verb: ne le lui dis pas. The hyphenated order after the verb is only for affirmative commands.

questions.stem: What does "Je fais réparer ma voiture" mean?
choices: I'm letting my car be repaired by a friend.
questions.explanation: Faire + infinitive means getting someone else to do it: I'm having my car repaired. "I'm repairing my car" is je répare ma voiture; "let" is laisser.

questions.stem: Replace "ma voiture" with a pronoun: "Je fais réparer ma voiture." → "Je ___ réparer."
questions.explanation: With faire + infinitive, the pronoun goes before faire: je la fais réparer. "Fais-la" is only for a command (Fais-la réparer !), and voiture is feminine (la).

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle s'est ___ couper les cheveux."
questions.explanation: Before an infinitive, fait never agrees, even with être and a feminine subject: elle s'est fait couper les cheveux.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les photos ? Je te les ai ___ hier."
questions.explanation: Les (les photos, feminine plural) is a direct object before avoir, so the participle agrees, even with te in between: envoyées.

questions.stem: How do you say "It's late, I'm leaving"?
choices: Il est tard, je me vais.
Il est tard, je m'en vais.
Il est tard, je m'y vais.
Il est tard, je m'en va.
questions.explanation: S'en aller (to go away, leave) keeps en: je m'en vais, tu t'en vas, il s'en va. "Je m'en va" uses the il form.

questions.stem: Before a plumber starts work, he gives you "un devis". What is it?
questions.explanation: Le devis is the quote, the price estimated before the work. The bill after the work is la facture.

questions.stem: The heel of your boot is broken. Where do you take it?
questions.explanation: Le cordonnier repairs shoes. Le pressing cleans clothes, le serrurier deals with locks and le plombier with water pipes and leaks.

questions.stem: Read: "Au garage, le mécanicien m'a dit que deux pneus étaient usés, alors je les ai fait changer aussi." Who changed the tyres?
choices: nobody: the tyres were only checked
questions.explanation: Je les ai fait changer = I had them changed: faire + infinitive means someone else, here the garage, did the work. Fait doesn't agree before an infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Le comes before lui (je le lui ai donné); m'en and donne-le-moi follow the rules. "Lui le" is the wrong order (and le would elide), and with faire + infinitive the pronoun goes before faire: je la fais réparer.

questions.stem: Replace both objects with pronouns: "J'ai envoyé la facture au client." → "Je ___ ai envoyée."
questions.explanation: La facture → la (column 2); au client → lui (column 3); la before lui, before the auxiliary: je la lui ai envoyée. Envoyée agrees with la.

questions.stem: Write the command "Give them to her!" (les clés), with the tu form of donner.
questions.explanation: Affirmative command: verb, then the direct object (les), then the person (lui), joined by hyphens: Donne-les-lui ! The tu form of an -er verb has no s: donne.

questions.stem: Put in order: "I didn't tell him (it)."
questions.explanation: Je ne le lui ai pas dit. The two pronouns stay together before the auxiliary (le before lui), and ne … pas goes around them and the auxiliary.

questions.stem: Match each problem to the person you call.
questions.explanation: A leak → the plumber; a broken lock → the locksmith; a haircut → the hairdresser; an oil change → the mechanic. Le cordonnier repairs shoes, l'électricien deals with wiring.

questions.stem: Name the numbered shops in this street.

image.alt: A street of five shops with blank signs and five numbered shop windows: scissors and a comb, a car on a ramp with a spanner, a shirt on a hanger, a boot, and a big key.

questions.explanation: Scissors and a comb: le coiffeur. A car on a ramp: le garage. A shirt on a hanger: le pressing (dry cleaner's). A boot: le cordonnier. A key: le serrurier (locksmith).

questions.stem: Complete: "Je n'aime ___ le thé ___ le café."
questions.explanation: Neither … nor is ne … ni … ni, with no pas: je n'aime ni le thé ni le café. The definite articles stay.

questions.stem: Make it negative: "J'ai un frère et une sœur."
choices: Je n'ai ni un frère ni une sœur.
Je n'ai pas ni frère ni sœur.
Je n'ai ni frère ni sœur.
Je n'ai ni de frère ni de sœur.
questions.explanation: After ni, un, une, des and du disappear: ni frère ni sœur. There's no pas with ni … ni.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the correct written French for "Neither Paul nor Léa came"?
choices: Ni Paul ni Léa sont venus.
Ni Paul ni Léa ne sont venus.
Ni Paul ni Léa ne sont pas venus.
Paul ni Léa ne sont venus.
questions.explanation: When ni … ni is the subject, each name gets ni and ne stays before the verb, without pas. The verb is usually plural.

questions.stem: What does "Tu dis n'importe quoi !" mean?
choices: You can say whatever you like.
questions.explanation: N'importe quoi = anything at all, and, as a criticism, nonsense: Tu dis n'importe quoi ! = You're talking nonsense!

questions.stem: What does "Il ne mange guère" mean?
questions.explanation: Ne … guère = hardly, scarcely (written, careful French). In speech: il ne mange presque pas.

questions.stem: A friend says "Ce film est nul !" What does she mean?
choices: The film is neither good nor bad.
questions.explanation: After être, nul is the informal adjective "useless, rubbish". The formal nul (no one) goes with ne and a verb: nul ne sait.

questions.stem: What does "Nul ne sait ce qui s'est passé" mean?
choices: Nothing is known about it at all.
He doesn't know anything about it.
Nobody wants to know what happened.
questions.explanation: Formal nul + ne = no one (personne ne … in everyday French): No one knows what happened.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle connaît la ville mieux que ___."
questions.explanation: Mieux que quiconque = better than anyone. Quelconque is an adjective after a noun, nul needs ne and a verb, and n'importe needs a question word (n'importe qui).

questions.stem: Complete: "Le restaurant était fermé pour une raison ___."
questions.explanation: Quelconque, after the noun, means "some … or other": pour une raison quelconque. Quiconque is a pronoun (whoever), aucune goes before the noun and needs a negative (pour aucune raison), and n'importe needs quel before the noun (pour n'importe quelle raison).

questions.stem: Complete: "Pas un seul client ___ venu."
questions.explanation: Pas un seul as the subject still needs ne before the verb, and pas is already there: Pas un seul client n'est venu.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Je ne bois ni thé ni café.
Ni Marc ni Julie ne travaillent ici.
Je n'aime pas ni le jazz ni le rap.
questions.explanation: Ni … ni with no article (thé, café) and with ne before a plural verb (ni Marc ni Julie ne travaillent) are right, and sans takes a noun without an article. N'importe quoi needs no ne, and ni … ni can't be combined with pas.

questions.stem: Make it negative with ni … ni: "Elle parle anglais et allemand." → "Elle ___ anglais ___ allemand."
questions.explanation: Ne before the verb, ni before each language, no pas: Elle ne parle ni anglais ni allemand.

questions.stem: Match each English expression to its French equivalent.
questions.explanation: N'importe + question word = any … at all: qui (person), où (place), quand (time), comment (way). Nulle part is nowhere and quelque part somewhere.

questions.stem: Put in order: "Neither the room nor the breakfast was worth the price."
questions.explanation: Ni la chambre ni le petit-déjeuner ne valaient le prix. Each subject gets ni, and ne goes before the (plural) verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ tour Eiffel a été construite en un peu plus de deux ans."
questions.explanation: A tower is la tour (feminine), which is also why the participle is construite. Le tour (masculine) is a turn or a trip around.

questions.stem: "La cathédrale a été restaurée de 1844 à 1864." Which form is "a été restaurée"?
questions.explanation: A été (passé composé of être) + restaurée (agreeing with la cathédrale) is the passé composé passive: the cathedral was restored.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, when did the fire at Notre-Dame happen?
questions.explanation: The fire was on 15 April 2019. The new cockerel was put on the spire on 16 December 2023, the cathedral reopened on 7 December 2024, and 1862 is when it was listed as a historic monument.

questions.stem: Why was the Eiffel Tower built?
questions.explanation: It was built for the Exposition universelle of 1889, which celebrated the centenary of the Revolution. Its scientific uses, especially radio, came later and saved it from demolition.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le projet a été critiqué par des artistes, parmi ___ Charles Garnier."
questions.explanation: After parmi, French uses lesquels / lesquelles, even for people: parmi lesquels (artistes, masculine plural).

questions.stem: What is the plural of "le vitrail"?
questions.explanation: Le vitrail becomes les vitraux, like le travail / les travaux.

questions.stem: What does "Notre-Dame a été classée monument historique en 1862" mean?
choices: It was ranked the best monument in 1862.
It was closed to the public in 1862.
Its documents were classified as secret in 1862.
It was listed as a protected historic monument in 1862.
questions.explanation: Classé monument historique = listed (protected by law) as a historic monument, the highest level of protection in France.

questions.stem: "Ma sœur travaille dans la restauration : elle est cuisinière dans un bistrot." What does "la restauration" mean here?
questions.explanation: La restauration has two meanings: restoring buildings or paintings, and the restaurant and catering trade. A cook in a bistro works in the second.

questions.stem: What is the Eiffel Tower made of, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: The tower is made of puddled iron (le fer puddlé), not steel: about 7,300 tonnes of it. The oak roof frame belonged to Notre-Dame.

questions.stem: Complete: "La flèche a été ___ à l'identique."
questions.explanation: In the passive the participle agrees with the subject: la flèche (feminine singular) → reconstruite.

questions.stem: Which statements are true, according to the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: The Eiffel Tower is classée monument historique.
With its antennas, the Eiffel Tower is now 330 metres high.
The Eiffel Tower was finished in 1900.
questions.explanation: Notre-Dame was begun in 1163 and reopened on 7 December 2024; the tower is 330 m with its antennas. The tower is only inscrite (a lower level of protection), not classée, and it was finished on 31 March 1889.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Eiffel a trouvé des usages scientifiques grâce ___ la tour a été sauvée."
questions.explanation: Grâce à + lesquels (usages, masculine plural) contracts to auxquels: des usages grâce auxquels la tour a été sauvée.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this cathedral.

image.alt: A side view of a Gothic cathedral with five numbered parts: a tall square tower on the left, wooden beams inside a cut-away roof, a thin pointed spire, a large round coloured window, and blocks of the wall on the right.

questions.explanation: 1 is the tower (la tour). 2 is the timber frame inside the roof (la charpente). 3 is the spire (la flèche). 4 is the stained-glass rose window (le vitrail). 5 shows the blocks the walls are built of (la pierre).

questions.stem: Put these events in the history of Notre-Dame in order, earliest first.
choices: Le roman de Victor Hugo paraît.
questions.explanation: Construction began in 1163, Victor Hugo's novel came out in 1831, the fire was on 15 April 2019, and the cathedral reopened on 7 December 2024.

questions.stem: Last Monday Paul said: « Je suis malade aujourd'hui. » Complete the report: "Lundi dernier, Paul m'a dit qu'il ___ malade ce jour-là."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb (a dit), the present becomes the imparfait: je suis → il était. "Ce jour-là" shows the day is over, so the present "est" doesn't fit. "Avait été" would report « J'ai été malade », and "serait" would report a futur.

questions.stem: « J'ai perdu mes clés. » In standard written French: "Elle a expliqué qu'elle ___ ses clés."
questions.explanation: The passé composé becomes the plus-que-parfait: j'ai perdu → elle avait perdu. "A perdu" is heard in relaxed speech but isn't the written standard; "perdait" would report « Je perdais »; "aurait perdu" is a conditionnel passé.

questions.stem: Last month Marc said: « Je viendrai samedi. » Complete: "Le mois dernier, Marc a dit qu'il ___ le samedi suivant."
questions.explanation: The futur becomes the conditionnel présent, the "future in the past": je viendrai → il viendrait. That Saturday is already past ("le samedi suivant"), so the futur "viendra" doesn't fit. "Venait" and "était venu" report other tenses.

questions.stem: Two years ago Inès said: « Je vais déménager le mois prochain. » Complete: "Il y a deux ans, Inès m'a annoncé qu'elle ___ déménager le mois suivant."
questions.explanation: The futur proche (va + infinitive) becomes aller in the imparfait + infinitive: elle allait déménager. "Va" ignores the shift; "irait déménager" would mean "would go and move"; "était allée" is a plus-que-parfait of aller.

questions.stem: « J'étais fatigué. » Which report is correct after "Il a dit …"?
questions.explanation: The imparfait doesn't change: j'étais → il était. "Avait été" would report « J'ai été fatigué »; "serait" a futur; "a été" is a passé composé.

questions.stem: On 3 May Léo said: « Je pars demain. » A month later you report it: "Léo m'a dit qu'il partait ___."
questions.explanation: Reported later, "demain" no longer means tomorrow, so it becomes le lendemain (the day after that day). La veille is the day before; ce jour-là is the same day.

questions.stem: Your friend said: « Hier, j'ai vu ton frère. » A week later you report it: "Elle m'a dit qu'elle avait vu mon frère ___."
questions.explanation: Hier becomes la veille (the day before) when the moment has passed. Hier would mean the day before today; le lendemain is the day after.

questions.stem: Which reporting verb tells the listener that the speaker doubts the claim?
questions.explanation: Prétendre means "to claim", and choosing it suggests you don't quite believe the claim (it doesn't mean "to pretend"). Affirmer states firmly, confirmer says something is true as expected, préciser adds a detail.

questions.stem: « C'est moi qui ai cassé le vase », a reconnu Tom. What did Tom do?
questions.explanation: Reconnaître que / reconnaître + a fact means "to admit". It also means "to recognise" a person or a place, but not here. To deny is nier; a doubtful claim is prétendre.

questions.stem: In written French, which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: After a quotation the subject comes after the verb, with -t- between two vowels: a-t-il répliqué. In the passé composé the pronoun goes after the auxiliary, not after the participle, and the participle is répliqué, not the infinitive.

questions.stem: Read: "La porte-parole a reconnu que le train était arrivé avec trois heures de retard. En revanche, elle a nié avoir laissé les voyageurs sans eau." What did the spokeswoman deny?
choices: that the train was three hours late
that the passengers would be refunded
questions.explanation: Nier + infinitive = to deny doing something: elle a nié avoir laissé les voyageurs sans eau. The delay is what she admitted (a reconnu); the breakdown and refunds aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: « Il faut que tu partes. » Complete: "Il m'a dit qu'il fallait que je ___."
questions.explanation: Only the main verb shifts (il faut → il fallait). The subjunctive after il fallait que stays a subjonctif présent: que je parte. Partais and partirais aren't subjunctives; sois parti is a subjonctif passé, for an earlier action.

questions.stem: Marc has just said: « Je viendrai demain. » You pass it on at once: "Marc dit qu'il ___ demain."
questions.explanation: The reporting verb dit is in the present, so nothing shifts: the futur stays viendra. The shifts (venait, était venu) only happen after a past reporting verb; vienne is a subjunctive, which dire que doesn't take when it reports a statement.

questions.stem: Write the missing verb (one word). « Je partirai à midi. » → "Elle a dit qu'elle ___ à midi."
questions.explanation: The futur becomes the conditionnel présent after a past reporting verb: je partirai → elle partirait.

questions.stem: Write the missing verb (two words). « J'ai oublié mon parapluie. » → "Il a dit qu'il ___ son parapluie."
questions.explanation: The passé composé becomes the plus-que-parfait: j'ai oublié → il avait oublié (imparfait of avoir + participle).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "She said she had already eaten."
questions.explanation: Elle a dit qu'elle avait déjà mangé. Déjà goes between the auxiliary avait and the participle, as in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Match each tense in direct speech with what it becomes after « il a dit que … ».
questions.explanation: Présent → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, futur → conditionnel, va + infinitive → allait + infinitive. The imparfait (like the plus-que-parfait and the conditionnel) doesn't change.

questions.stem: Which tenses stay the same in reported speech after « il a dit que … »? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The imparfait, the plus-que-parfait and the conditionnel are already "past" or hypothetical, so they don't move. The présent becomes the imparfait, the passé composé the plus-que-parfait and the futur the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Malik spoke on Tuesday. Name each numbered day as you'd say it when reporting his words later.

image.alt: A timeline from Sunday to Thursday. Malik's speech bubble on Tuesday says « Je suis parti hier et je reviens demain. » Five numbered boxes sit under the five days, and a box at the bottom reports his words on Saturday.

questions.explanation: Seen from Tuesday: Sunday is deux jours plus tôt, Monday la veille, Tuesday ce jour-là, Wednesday le lendemain, Thursday deux jours plus tard. Hier and demain only work from today's point of view.

questions.stem: « Tu as vu le voleur ? » Complete: "Le policier m'a demandé ___ j'avais vu le voleur."
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si. Si only becomes s' before il and ils, so si j'avais vu. Que introduces a statement, and ce que replaces "what".

questions.stem: Last week a police officer stopped you at a roadblock: « Où allez-vous ? » In standard French: "Il m'a demandé ___."
questions.explanation: A reported question has statement word order: no est-ce que and no inversion. After the past verb a demandé, the present shifts to the imparfait: où j'allais. Où je vais would only be possible in speech for a trip still going on, and this one is over.

questions.stem: « Qu'est-ce que vous avez vu ? » Complete: "Elle m'a demandé ___ j'avais vu."
questions.explanation: Qu'est-ce que becomes ce que in a reported question. Ce qui is for "what" as the subject; here je is the subject, so "what" is the object.

questions.stem: « Qu'est-ce qui s'est passé ? » In standard French: "Il voulait savoir ___."
questions.explanation: "What" is the subject (no other subject follows), so ce qui; and the passé composé shifts to the plus-que-parfait after the past verb voulait savoir.

questions.stem: After last year's burglary the officer asked: « Porterez-vous plainte ? » Complete: "L'agent m'a demandé si je ___ plainte."
questions.explanation: Si here means "whether", so it can take the conditionnel: the futur porterez becomes the conditionnel porterais. Porterai doesn't shift (and the decision is long past); portais would report « Vous portez plainte ? ».

questions.stem: « Ne bougez pas ! » In standard French: "Le policier nous a dit ___."
questions.explanation: A negative order becomes de + ne pas + infinitive, with ne pas together before the infinitive. Dropping ne is casual speech; the imperative bougez can't follow de.

questions.stem: Julie tells Marc: « Rappelle-moi ! » Complete: "Julie a dit à Marc de ___."
questions.explanation: The order becomes de + infinitive, and moi (Julie) becomes la: de la rappeler. Le would mean Marc himself; me would mean the person telling the story.

questions.stem: Complete (her = Anna, him = Tom): "Anna ___ a supplié de rester."
questions.explanation: Supplier takes a direct object: supplier quelqu'un de faire quelque chose, so l' (le). Lui is for verbs with à, such as demander à or dire à.

questions.stem: Complete (him = the driver): "Le policier ___ a ordonné de s'arrêter."
questions.explanation: Ordonner takes à + the person: ordonner à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose, so the pronoun is lui. L' and le are for direct objects (as with supplier).

questions.stem: « Non, je ne signerai pas ce constat ! » Sum it up: "Il a ___ signer le constat."
questions.explanation: Saying no to signing is refusing: il a refusé de signer. Accepter de is the opposite, promettre de a promise, menacer de a threat.

questions.stem: Read: "Un policier qui passait s'est arrêté. Il nous a demandé si quelqu'un était blessé, puis il nous a conseillé de remplir un constat amiable." What did the officer advise?
choices: to go to the police station
to take the cars to a garage
to fill in an accident report
questions.explanation: Il nous a conseillé de remplir un constat amiable: he advised them to fill in the joint accident report. He also asked whether anyone was hurt; the other options aren't in the text.

questions.stem: In an insurance contract, what is "la franchise"?
choices: the part of the damage you pay yourself
the form the drivers fill in
the yearly price of the insurance
questions.explanation: La franchise is the excess (US: deductible): the amount you pay yourself. Compensation is l'indemnisation, the form is le constat. (Outside insurance, la franchise also means frankness.)

questions.stem: Where do you go in a French town to report a theft and press charges?
questions.explanation: You porter plainte at le commissariat (police station), or at the gendarmerie in the countryside. Le constat is the accident form, le sinistre an insurance claim, and the insurer (l'assureur) is told afterwards.

questions.stem: Write the missing verb (one word). « Où étiez-vous à 22 heures ? » → "Il m'a demandé où j'___ à 22 heures."
questions.explanation: The imparfait étiez stays in the imparfait; only the person changes: vous étiez → j'étais.

questions.stem: Write the missing word. « Vous viendrez à la réunion ? » → "Il m'a demandé ___ je viendrais à la réunion."
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si (whether). Because si means "whether" here, the conditionnel viendrais is correct after it.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "He asked me what I wanted."
questions.explanation: Il m'a demandé ce que je voulais. "What" as an object is ce que, followed by statement order: subject, then verb (in the imparfait after the past reporting verb).

questions.stem: Match each direct question with the word that starts it when it is reported.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions take si; qu'est-ce que becomes ce que; qu'est-ce qui becomes ce qui; question words like où stay. Est-ce que never appears in a reported question.

questions.stem: Which reported sentences are correct in standard French? Select all that apply.
choices: Il m'a demandé si j'avais fini.
Elle nous a dit de ne pas toucher à la voiture.
Il m'a demandé ce que je voulais.
Il m'a demandé où est-ce que j'habitais.
Elle lui a supplié de rester.
questions.explanation: The first three follow the rules (si + shifted tense; de ne pas + infinitive; ce que). Est-ce que is never kept in a reported question (où j'habitais), and supplier takes a direct object (elle l'a supplié de rester).

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this accident scene.

image.alt: A minor accident at a roundabout with five numbered things: a two-column form on the bonnet of a red car, a dent in the door of a blue car, a man on the pavement pointing at the cars, a police officer with a notebook, and a round central island with a tree.

questions.explanation: The form both drivers sign is le constat (amiable); the dent is les dégâts (damage); the man who saw it is le témoin; the officer is le policier; the island is part of le rond-point. La franchise and l'assureur aren't things you can see.

questions.stem: « Pourquoi tu fermes les volets ? — ___ il fait trop chaud. »
questions.explanation: Only parce que answers the question Pourquoi ? Puisque and vu que give a reason that is already known, so they can't answer a question about it; comme must come before a main clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ tu es là, aide-moi à porter les bouteilles d'eau."
questions.explanation: Puisque gives a reason the listener can see (you're here), and it can start the sentence. Car can't come first with its cause, and à cause de, grâce à need a noun, not a clause.

questions.stem: Complete the sign: "La randonnée est annulée ___ la canicule."
questions.explanation: En raison de + noun is the formal "due to", typical of announcements. Puisque and sous prétexte que need a clause, and si bien que introduces a consequence, not a cause.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ temps, nous n'avons pas visité le parc naturel." (for lack of time)
questions.explanation: Faute de + a noun with no article: faute de temps. À force de is for something repeated; grâce à gives a good cause, which doesn't fit missing the park.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il a tellement plu ___ la rivière a débordé."
questions.explanation: Tellement (or si, tant) is completed by que: tellement plu que … Si bien que is a separate connector, and donc doesn't follow tellement.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il y avait ___ fumée qu'on ne voyait plus la route."
questions.explanation: Before a noun, use tellement de or tant de: tellement de fumée. Si only goes before an adjective or an adverb, and tellement alone needs de before a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il a ___ plu que les routes étaient fermées."
questions.explanation: With a verb, use tellement or tant, between the auxiliary and the participle: il a tellement plu. Si and très go with adjectives and adverbs, and de is only for nouns.

questions.stem: Which connector fits best in a formal report? "Les nappes d'eau sont très basses ; ___, l'arrosage est interdit."
questions.explanation: Par conséquent is the written, formal way to give a consequence. Du coup means the same but is spoken and casual; puisque and sous prétexte que introduce causes.

questions.stem: "Il ne trie pas ses déchets sous prétexte qu'il n'a pas le temps." What does the speaker think?
choices: that the reason is true and well known
that he has plenty of time
that the reason is just an excuse
that he sorts his rubbish carefully
questions.explanation: Sous prétexte que reports someone's reason while hinting that it's an excuse. A reason that is true and known would take puisque.

questions.stem: What does this mean? "À force d'arroser tous les jours, il a sauvé ses tomates."
choices: For lack of watering, he lost his tomatoes.
Despite watering every day, he lost his tomatoes.
Instead of watering, he picked his tomatoes.
By watering every day, he saved his tomatoes.
questions.explanation: À force de + infinitive gives a cause that is repeated: by watering again and again. For lack of is faute de; despite is malgré; instead of is au lieu de.

questions.stem: Read: "Selon une étude de l'Inserm, la vague de chaleur a provoqué environ 14 800 décès de plus que d'habitude entre le 1er et le 20 août 2003." Which statement is true?
choices: About 14,800 more people died than usual in the first twenty days of August 2003.
About 14,800 people died in France in the whole of 2003.
The study found fewer deaths than usual.
questions.explanation: De plus que d'habitude = more than usual, and the period is 1 to 20 August. The figure counts extra deaths, not all deaths in the year.

questions.stem: Complete (= caused): "Un barbecue mal éteint a ___ l'incendie."
questions.explanation: Provoquer = to cause, often something sudden or bad. Conserver is to keep, éviter to avoid, souligner to stress.

questions.stem: What is "la sécheresse"?
questions.explanation: La sécheresse (from sec, dry) is a drought. A heatwave is la canicule, a flood l'inondation, global warming le réchauffement climatique.

questions.stem: Write the missing word (for lack of): "___ d'eau, les fleurs sont mortes."
questions.explanation: Faute de + noun without an article: faute d'eau = for lack of water.

questions.stem: Write one word meaning "so": "Il faisait ___ chaud qu'on a dormi dehors."
questions.explanation: Before an adjective (chaud), use si or tellement, completed by que: si chaud que, tellement chaud que. Tant only goes with a verb (or tant de with a noun).

questions.stem: Put the parts in order: "It didn't rain, with the result that the river has dried up."
questions.explanation: Il n'a pas plu, si bien que la rivière est à sec. Si bien que comes after the cause (and a comma) and introduces the result; it can't start the sentence.

questions.stem: Match each connector with the register it suits best.
questions.explanation: Du coup and vu que are typical of speech; c'est pourquoi (like donc) is neutral; par conséquent and en raison de belong to written, formal French.

questions.stem: Which of these can be followed directly by a noun? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: En raison de, faute de and à cause de take a noun (en raison de la chaleur, faute de temps, à cause de la pluie). Puisque and si bien que introduce a clause with a verb.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this summer landscape.

image.alt: A summer landscape with five numbered things: a thermometer showing 42 °C next to the sun, a dry riverbed with cracked earth, a factory chimney giving off smoke, flames on a forested hill, and a frog beside an almost empty pond under a warning sign.

choices: les gaz à effet de serre
questions.explanation: 42 °C is la canicule; the cracked, dry riverbed shows la sécheresse; the smoke from the chimney (and the car) stands for les gaz à effet de serre; the flames are an incendie; the frog by its vanishing pond is une espèce menacée. There's no flood (inondation) or storm (tempête) in the picture.

questions.stem: Complete: "Bien qu'il ___ fatigué, il a préparé le dîner."
questions.explanation: Bien que always takes the subjunctive: bien qu'il soit. Est, était and sera are indicative forms (they would follow même si, except the futur).

questions.stem: Complete: "Même s'il ___ fatigué, il prépare le dîner."
questions.explanation: Même si takes the indicative, and like si it never takes the futur or the conditionnel straight after it: même s'il est fatigué. Soit would follow bien que.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ la pluie, on a déjeuné dehors."
questions.explanation: Malgré + noun: malgré la pluie. Bien que and même si need a clause with a verb; cependant is an adverb that starts a new clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai ___ essayer, je n'arrive pas à faire une bonne mayonnaise."
questions.explanation: Avoir beau + infinitive, and beau never changes: j'ai beau essayer = no matter how hard I try.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses opposition (two different facts side by side) rather than concession?
choices: Bien qu'il soit pressé, il prend le temps de déjeuner.
Il a beau manger, il a toujours faim.
Malgré la pluie, on est sortis.
Mon frère mange de la viande, alors que ma sœur est végétarienne.
questions.explanation: Alors que compares two facts; you could swap them round. The others break an expectation (being in a hurry, eating, the rain should have led to something else): that's concession.

questions.stem: Which is the most formal way to say "however"?
questions.explanation: Néanmoins (like toutefois) is formal and mostly written. Mais bon and quand même are spoken; pourtant is neutral.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ son frère, Léa adore cuisiner."
questions.explanation: Contrairement à + noun = unlike. Alors que needs a clause with a verb; "contrairement que" doesn't exist; en revanche starts a new clause and isn't followed by a noun like this.

questions.stem: "Certes, ce plat est cher, mais il est délicieux." What does certes do here?
choices: It gives the reason for the price.
