It grants a point before an objection.
questions.explanation: Certes (admittedly) accepts a point (it's expensive) before mais answers it (but it's delicious). It's the classic first step of a counter-argument.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les jeunes achètent des plats cuisinés, ___ leurs grands-parents cuisinaient tout eux-mêmes."
questions.explanation: Two habits side by side: opposition, so tandis que (or alors que) + indicative. Bien que would need a subjunctive and means "although"; malgré needs a noun; avoir beau an infinitive.

questions.stem: What is "le terroir"?
choices: a farming area with its soil, climate and local produce
a large territory with no towns
a ready meal from the supermarket
questions.explanation: Le terroir is a local farming area and what it produces: les produits du terroir are local specialities. A ready meal is un plat cuisiné.

questions.stem: Read: "Selon l'Insee, en 2010, les adultes passaient en moyenne 2 h 22 par jour à manger, soit 13 minutes de plus qu'en 1986." Which statement is true?
choices: Adults spent less time eating in 2010 than in 1986.
Adults spent more time eating in 2010 than in 1986.
Adults spent 13 minutes a day eating in 2010.
Adults spent the same time eating in both years.
questions.explanation: 13 minutes de plus = 13 minutes more: 2 h 22 in 2010 against 2 h 09 in 1986. That's why the text starts with pourtant: the figures contradict the idea that the French eat faster and faster.

questions.stem: What does "démodé" mean?
questions.explanation: Démodé = out of fashion (dé- + la mode). Trendy is à la mode or tendance.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il était fatigué, mais il a ___ préparé le dîner."
questions.explanation: Tout de même (= quand même) goes after the auxiliary: il a tout de même préparé = he made dinner all the same. Contrairement needs à + noun, alors que a clause, malgré a noun.

questions.stem: Write the missing word: "Elle a ___ chercher, elle ne trouve pas ses clés." (no matter how hard she looks)
questions.explanation: Avoir beau + infinitive: elle a beau chercher. Beau never agrees, even with elle.

questions.stem: Write one word meaning "whereas": "Paul aime la ville, ___ que sa sœur préfère la campagne."
questions.explanation: Alors que and tandis que both put two facts side by side, + indicative.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "However much she tasted the sauce …"
questions.explanation: Elle avait beau goûter la sauce (…, elle ne reconnaissait pas l'épice). Avoir is conjugated, then beau, then the infinitive and its object.

questions.stem: Match each connector with what follows it.
questions.explanation: Bien que (and quoique) + subjunctive; même si + indicative; malgré + noun; avoir beau + infinitive. None of them is followed by the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Which of these express concession (an expectation that is broken)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Bien que, avoir beau and pourtant all say that something should have stopped the result but didn't. Tandis que and en revanche simply set two facts side by side: opposition.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the "then and now" picture.

image.alt: Two panels with five numbered things. Left, autrefois: a family round a table with a big cooking pot. Right, aujourd'hui: a plastic tray with a film lid next to a microwave; a burger, fries and a paper cup; a plate of vegetables and lentils; a market basket with a round cheese, a loaf and a jar marked AOP.

questions.explanation: The pot on the family table is le repas de famille; the tray for the microwave is a plat cuisiné; the burger and fries are le fast-food; vegetables and lentils make un plat végétarien; local cheese and the AOP jar are les produits du terroir. La mode and la tendance are ideas, not things in the picture.

questions.stem: Which register is this? « T'as vu le match ? C'était ouf ! »
questions.explanation: T'as (for tu as) and the verlan word ouf mark relaxed, informal speech.

questions.stem: What is the neutral word for "la bagnole"?
questions.explanation: La bagnole is informal for la voiture. Le véhicule is the formal word (in official letters); la bouffe is informal for food.

questions.stem: What does "J'ai la flemme de sortir" mean?
choices: I'm in a hurry to go out.
I can't be bothered to go out.
I've got a temperature, so I'm staying in.
questions.explanation: Avoir la flemme (de + infinitive) is informal for not feeling like doing something out of laziness.

questions.stem: What is the verlan form of "fou"?
questions.explanation: Fou swapped round gives ouf. Relou comes from lourd, chelou from louche, meuf from femme.

questions.stem: "Relou" (annoying) is verlan for which word?
questions.explanation: Lourd (heavy, tiresome), said "lou-re", is turned round into re-lou. Chelou comes from louche, ouf from fou.

questions.stem: Which verb is the formal equivalent of "aller" in a letter? ("Je ___ à la mairie lundi.")
questions.explanation: Se rendre is the formal "to go (somewhere)": Je me rendrai à la mairie. Bouger and filer are informal; partir means to leave, not to go to a place.

questions.stem: Which sentence fits a letter to the town hall?
choices: Mon pote m'a dit de vous écrire.
Je vous prie de m'excuser pour ce retard.
Je bosse le samedi, c'est pas possible.
questions.explanation: Only the third is formal (vous, je vous prie de, ne kept). La flemme, mon pote, je bosse and c'est pas are informal.

questions.stem: What is the neutral equivalent of "kiffer"?
questions.explanation: Kiffer (informal, young people's speech) means to love or be really into something: adorer, aimer beaucoup. Bosser is informal for travailler.

questions.stem: Which sentence is informal because of its grammar, not its words?
questions.explanation: Dropping ne is typical of informal speech. Ce n'est pas grave is neutral; cela is more careful; fut (passé simple) is written, even literary.

questions.stem: How would you describe "chouette" (C'était une chouette soirée)?
choices: informal and a bit old-fashioned, meaning "great, nice"
questions.explanation: Chouette is informal and sounds a little dated (more parents than teenagers). It isn't rude and it isn't verlan. As a noun, la chouette is an owl.

questions.stem: Write the neutral word for "le boulot", with its article.
questions.explanation: Le boulot is informal for le travail (work) or l'emploi (a job).

questions.stem: Match each informal word with its neutral equivalent.
questions.explanation: Le fric = l'argent, la bouffe = la nourriture, bosser = travailler, le pote = l'ami (or le copain). La voiture is the neutral word for la bagnole.

questions.stem: Which of these words are informal? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Le fric, la bagnole and kiffer are labelled familier in dictionaries. L'argent and travailler are their neutral equivalents.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I won't be able to join you." (formal)
questions.explanation: Je ne pourrai pas me joindre à vous. In formal French ne is always kept, and ne … pas surround the conjugated verb pourrai; the pronoun me stays with the infinitive joindre.

questions.stem: What does "J'ai le cafard" mean?
questions.explanation: Avoir le cafard = to feel low, to have the blues. Cockroaches in the kitchen would be des cafards; being lazy is avoir un poil dans la main.

questions.stem: What does "Il m'a posé un lapin" mean?
choices: He played a trick on me.
questions.explanation: Poser un lapin à quelqu'un = to not turn up for a date or meeting. Telling lies is raconter des salades; playing a trick is faire marcher.

questions.stem: Which idiom means "to faint"?
choices: avoir un poil dans la main
questions.explanation: Tomber dans les pommes = to faint (neutral: s'évanouir). Avoir un poil dans la main is to be lazy, être dans la lune to daydream, casser les pieds to annoy.

questions.stem: How do you say "It's raining cats and dogs"?
choices: Il pleut des chats et des chiens.
questions.explanation: French rain falls in ropes: il pleut des cordes (or il pleut à verse). The English image doesn't translate word for word.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je ne trouve pas la réponse, je donne ___ langue au chat."
questions.explanation: The possessive changes with the person: je donne ma langue au chat, tu donnes ta langue au chat. Sa is only for il or elle (or the infinitive form you look up).

questions.stem: "Ce téléphone m'a coûté les yeux de la tête." What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Coûter les yeux de la tête = to cost an arm and a leg.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what did people say in the 17th century instead of "donner sa langue au chat"?
choices: jeter son chat dans la rue
poser sa langue sur la table
questions.explanation: The older form was jeter sa langue aux chiens (Madame de Sévigné used it); in the 19th century the cat, a keeper of secrets, replaced the dogs.

questions.stem: Which idiom is neutral enough to use with your manager at work?
choices: avoir un poil dans la main
avoir du pain sur la planche
questions.explanation: Avoir du pain sur la planche (to have a lot to do) is neutral and very common at work. The other three are informal, and calling someone lazy or a liar is risky anyway.

questions.stem: How do you say "to pull someone's leg" (to tease them)?
questions.explanation: Faire marcher quelqu'un = to have someone on. "Tirer la jambe" is a word-for-word translation that French doesn't use; casser les pieds is to annoy; poser un lapin is to stand someone up.

questions.stem: « Ça m'a coûté les yeux de la tête. » Complete the report in standard French: "Il m'a dit que ça lui ___ les yeux de la tête."
questions.explanation: An idiom shifts like any verb: the passé composé a coûté becomes the plus-que-parfait avait coûté after il m'a dit (lesson 17). Coûtait would report « Ça me coûte ».

questions.stem: Complete the idiom meaning "to have a lot on your plate": "avoir du pain sur la ___"
questions.explanation: Avoir du pain sur la planche: la planche is a board. Bread kept on a board once meant you had food put by; today it means plenty of work ahead.

questions.stem: Match each idiom with its meaning.
left: mettre les pieds dans le plat
choices: to put your foot in it
questions.explanation: Être dans la lune = to have your head in the clouds; raconter des salades = to tell fibs; mettre les pieds dans le plat = to bring up the awkward subject; casser les pieds = to annoy. To faint is tomber dans les pommes.

questions.stem: According to the lesson's table, which of these idioms are informal? Select all that apply.
choices: avoir un poil dans la main
questions.explanation: Avoir un poil dans la main, tomber dans les pommes and raconter des salades are informal. Être dans la lune and il pleut des cordes are neutral.

questions.stem: Each numbered picture takes an idiom literally. Name the idiom.

image.alt: Five numbered cartoon panels: a hand with a long hair on its palm; a person falling into a pile of apples; rain falling as ropes from a cloud; a person sitting on a crescent moon; a rabbit sitting alone on a café chair with a clock on the wall.

choices: avoir un poil dans la main
questions.explanation: Each drawing shows the words of an idiom: a hair in the hand (lazy), falling into apples (fainting), rain as ropes (pouring), sitting on the moon (daydreaming), a rabbit left waiting at a café (being stood up).

questions.stem: Complete: "D'une part, le tram est rapide ; ___, il est bon marché."
questions.explanation: "D'une part" is always followed by "d'autre part": here both halves are points in favour of the tram. "Par contre" and "en revanche" announce a contrast, and "au contraire" contradicts, but "rapide" and "bon marché" don't contrast.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Il est non seulement cher, mais aussi très loin.
Il non seulement est cher, mais aussi très loin.
Il est non seulement cher, mais seulement très loin.
Il est seulement non cher, mais aussi très loin.
questions.explanation: "Non seulement … mais aussi" puts each half before the words it stresses: "non seulement cher, mais aussi très loin". "Non seulement" can't sit between the subject and the verb ("Il non seulement est"); "mais seulement" and "seulement non cher" make no sense.

questions.stem: Complete with "convaincre" in the present: "Ce film ne me ___ pas."
questions.explanation: "Il convainc" has no final -t: the c of the stem is enough. "Convaincs" is the je / tu form, and "convainque" is the subjunctive.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Je ne suis pas convaincu que cette mesure ___ efficace."
questions.explanation: A negative opinion ("je ne suis pas convaincu que", "je ne pense pas que") takes the subjunctive in writing: "qu'elle soit". "Est" is what you may hear in relaxed speech; "sois" is the wrong person (je / tu).

questions.stem: Which word fits? "Je ne crois pas à ce projet. ___, il a déjà échoué dans la ville voisine." (The second sentence backs up the first.)
questions.explanation: "D'ailleurs" adds something that supports what you have just said ("in fact"). "Ailleurs" alone means "elsewhere"; "par contre" and "au contraire" would announce a contrast.

questions.stem: Which phrase makes an opinion more careful?
questions.explanation: "Dans une certaine mesure" (to some extent) limits the claim: that is hedging. The other three make the claim stronger.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu arrives toujours en retard. La prochaine fois, pars ___ !"
questions.explanation: "Plus tôt" (earlier) is the opposite of "plus tard". "Plutôt" (rather) sounds exactly the same but means something else; "plus tard" would make the advice illogical.

questions.stem: "Beaucoup de villes, notamment les plus grandes, limitent les voitures." What does "notamment" mean here?
questions.explanation: "Notamment" picks out one case among others: "in particular, notably". "Nevertheless" is "néanmoins", "on the contrary" is "au contraire", "finally" is "enfin".

questions.stem: "Le médecin lui a défendu de faire du sport." What did the doctor do?
choices: He advised him to do sport.
He forbade him to do sport.
He helped him to do sport.
questions.explanation: "Défendre à quelqu'un de" + infinitive means "to forbid someone to", like "interdire". Its other meaning, "to defend", takes a direct object: "défendre son point de vue".

questions.stem: Complete: "___, les écrans peuvent aider les enfants à apprendre, mais ils les empêchent parfois de dormir."
questions.explanation: "Certes …, mais …" admits a point and then answers it. "Bref" sums up, "en outre" adds a point and "notamment" picks out an example: none of them prepares the "mais".

questions.stem: Read: "À mon avis, la semaine de quatre jours est plutôt une bonne idée, à condition que les journées ne soient pas trop longues. Il me semble que les salariés seraient moins fatigués. Je ne suis cependant pas convaincue qu'elle convienne à tous les métiers." What is the writer's position?
choices: She thinks it suits every job.
She is in favour, with a condition and some doubts.
questions.explanation: "Plutôt une bonne idée" is a position in favour; "à condition que" adds a condition and "je ne suis pas convaincue qu'elle convienne à tous les métiers" a doubt. Hedging is not the same as having no opinion.

questions.stem: Complete: "Une journaliste doit rester ___." (impartial)
questions.explanation: "Objectif" makes "objective" in the feminine, to agree with "une journaliste". "Subjective" means the opposite.

questions.stem: What does "Avant de décider, il faut peser le pour et le contre" mean?
choices: Before deciding, you have to take a position for or against.
Before deciding, you have to ask everyone's opinion.
Before deciding, you have to weigh up the pros and cons.
Before deciding, you have to count the votes.
questions.explanation: "Le pour et le contre" = the pros and cons; "peser" = to weigh.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il me semble que tu ___ raison."
questions.explanation: "Il me semble que" (it seems to me that) gives an opinion and takes the indicative, like "je pense que". Without "me", "il semble que" is more often followed by the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in standard written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Je pense que c'est une bonne idée.
Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
Je pense que ce soit une bonne idée.
Il me semble que c'est une bonne idée.
Je suis convaincu que ce soit une bonne idée.
questions.explanation: Affirmative opinion and certainty take the indicative: "je pense que c'est", "il me semble que c'est", "je suis convaincu que c'est". A negative opinion takes the subjunctive: "je ne pense pas que ce soit".

questions.stem: Type the missing words: "Le vélo est ___ bon pour la santé, ___ économique." (not only … but also)
questions.explanation: "Non seulement … mais aussi" (or "mais également", "mais encore"): each half goes before the word it stresses.

questions.stem: Put the sentences of this paragraph in order.
choices: Selon moi, il faut limiter les écrans chez les jeunes enfants.
Tout d'abord, ils les empêchent de bien dormir.
Par exemple, ma fille se couchait très tard quand elle avait une tablette dans sa chambre.
De plus, ils remplacent souvent le jeu et la lecture.
Bref, il ne faut pas interdire les écrans, mais il faut fixer des règles.
questions.explanation: The position comes first; "tout d'abord" opens the first argument, and its example (sleep) follows it at once; "de plus" adds the second argument; "bref" sums up at the end. "Ils" in the second sentence needs "les écrans" from the first.

questions.stem: Match each connector with its job.
questions.explanation: "Tout d'abord" opens the first point, "de plus" adds one, "par exemple" brings in an example, "certes" concedes a point before "mais", and "bref" sums up. None of them gives a cause ("parce que", "puisque" do that).

questions.stem: Which connector fits each numbered slot of this argumentative text?

image.alt: The skeleton of an argumentative text as six stacked boxes, each with an empty numbered slot for a connector: 1 Introduction, the question and your position; 2 Argument 1, your first reason; 3 Example, a fact, a case, an experience; 4 Argument 2, your second reason; 5 The other side, admit it, then answer it; 6 Conclusion, sum up, position again.

questions.explanation: 1 states your position ("pour ma part"), 2 opens the first argument ("tout d'abord"), 3 brings in its example ("par exemple"), 4 adds the second argument ("de plus"), 5 admits the other side and answers it ("certes … mais"), and 6 concludes ("en conclusion"). "Parce que" gives a cause and "c'est-à-dire" explains; neither structures a text.

questions.stem: In the DELF B1, what does the writing paper ask for?
choices: Two short messages of about 60 words each
One text giving your view, at least about 160 words
A letter of at least 500 words
questions.explanation: One text (an essay, a letter or an article) in which you give your view on a general topic, at least about 160 words in 45 minutes. Two short texts is the A2 paper. Always follow the instructions on the paper.

questions.stem: Which opening is right for a formal letter to someone you don't know?
questions.explanation: "Madame, Monsieur," (or the person's title: "Monsieur le Maire,") is the formal opening. "Cher ami" is for someone you know; "Salut" and "Coucou" are informal.

questions.stem: Complete: "Veuillez ___ ci-joint mon dossier."
questions.explanation: "Veuillez" (please, formal) is followed directly by an infinitive, with no "de" or "à": "Veuillez trouver ci-joint …".

questions.stem: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Right after its noun, "ci-joint" agrees like an adjective: "la facture ci-jointe", "les documents ci-joints". It stays unchanged only at the start of a sentence or before a noun without an article.

questions.stem: Which request suits a formal letter to the town council?
choices: Nous vous serions reconnaissants de bien vouloir limiter le bruit.
Hé, moins de bruit, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: The formal request uses "vous", the conditionnel ("nous vous serions reconnaissants") and "bien vouloir". "Tu pourrais …" is informal; the imperative and "Hé" are too direct for a letter.

questions.stem: Which is the nominalisation of "fermer l'usine"?
questions.explanation: "Fermer" gives "la fermeture" (-ure), and the object follows with "de": "la fermeture de l'usine". The other nouns don't exist.

questions.stem: What does "les riverains" mean in "Les riverains se plaignent du bruit"?
questions.explanation: "Les riverains" are the people who live in a particular street or along a road or river: the local residents. Councillors are "les élus".

questions.stem: Complete with "rédiger" in the present: "Nous ___ une pétition."
questions.explanation: Like "manger", "rédiger" keeps the e before -ons so that the g stays soft: "nous rédigeons". "Rédigez" is the vous form.

questions.stem: Who elects the mayor of a French town?
choices: the residents, in a separate vote
questions.explanation: The town's voters elect the conseil municipal (town council), and the council elects the mayor from among its members.

questions.stem: In a newspaper, what is "la rubrique"?
questions.explanation: "La rubrique" is a section or column: "la rubrique sport", "la rubrique Vie locale". The title is "le titre"; readers' letters go in "le courrier des lecteurs".

questions.stem: "Je vous remercie de la suite que vous donnerez à ma demande." What does the writer thank the reader for?
choices: the reply they have already sent
the action they will take on the request
questions.explanation: "La suite que vous donnerez à ma demande" is the follow-up, the action you will take on my request. "Donner suite à" = to follow up.

questions.stem: In the article about the swimming pool, why are some people unhappy?
choices: The entry price has gone up.
questions.explanation: "L'augmentation du prix de l'entrée, qui passe de 3 à 4 euros, ne fait pas l'unanimité." The water is warmer, the pool is reopening, and a children's pool has been created.

questions.stem: Which sentence does NOT belong in a formal letter to the mayor?
choices: Je me permets de vous écrire au sujet du bruit.
Je vous serais reconnaissante de bien vouloir intervenir.
Salut, je t'écris pour le bruit.
Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie d'agréer, Monsieur le Maire, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
questions.explanation: "Salut" and "tu" are informal: a formal letter keeps "vous" and formal phrases from the first line to the last.

questions.stem: Which phrases belong in a formal letter? Select all that apply.
choices: Je me permets de vous écrire
questions.explanation: "Je me permets de vous écrire", "Veuillez trouver ci-joint" and "Dans l'attente de votre réponse" are formal. "Bisous" (love, kisses) and "À plus !" (see you) are for friends.

questions.stem: Complete this newspaper title with the noun made from "améliorer" (no article): "___ de la sécurité devant l'école"
questions.explanation: "Améliorer" gives "l'amélioration" (-tion): "Amélioration de la sécurité devant l'école". Titles often drop the article.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this formal letter in order.
choices: Je me permets de vous écrire au sujet du bruit dans notre rue.
Veuillez trouver ci-joint la pétition des riverains.
Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
questions.explanation: The subject line comes before the opening; the body states why you write and then what you enclose; the closing formula and the signature end the letter.

questions.stem: Match each verb with its noun.
questions.explanation: "Arriver → l'arrivée" (-ée), "construire → la construction" (-tion), "augmenter → l'augmentation" (-tion), "baisser → la baisse" (the bare stem). "L'arrêt" is the noun of "arrêter".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this formal letter.

image.alt: The layout of a formal letter with grey bars instead of text and six numbered parts: 1 three short lines at the top left; 2 three lines on the right below them; 3 a short line before the body; 4 a very short line just before the body; 5 three lines after the three paragraphs of the body; 6 a short line at the bottom right.

questions.explanation: 1 the sender's address (l'expéditeur), top left; 2 the recipient (le destinataire), on the right; 3 the subject line (l'objet); 4 the opening (la formule d'appel); 5 the closing formula (la formule de politesse), after the body; 6 the signature (la signature). A letter has no "titre" or "chapeau": those are parts of an article.

questions.stem: Which is a polite way to interrupt someone?
questions.explanation: Apologise first, then say why: "Pardon de vous interrompre, mais …". "Tu me coupes la parole !" is a complaint about being interrupted, and "Laissez-moi finir" keeps the floor rather than taking it.

questions.stem: Complete with "interrompre" in the present: "Il ___ toujours les autres."
questions.explanation: "Interrompre" is like "rompre": "il interrompt", with a t. "Interromps" is the je / tu form and "interrompe" the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Je vois qu'est-ce que tu veux dire.
Je vois que tu veux dire.
Je vois ce qui tu veux dire.
Je vois ce que tu veux dire.
questions.explanation: In an indirect question, "qu'est-ce que" becomes "ce que" (lesson 18). "Ce qui" is a subject, and "que" alone changes the meaning ("I see that you want to say").

questions.stem: Complete: "On s'est mis d'accord ___ la date."
questions.explanation: You agree on something: "se mettre d'accord sur". You agree with someone: "être d'accord avec quelqu'un".

questions.stem: Which is the most polite way to disagree?
choices: Je ne serais pas tout à fait d'accord.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel ("je ne serais pas") and "pas tout à fait" soften the disagreement. The others are blunt, and "Tu dis n'importe quoi" (you're talking nonsense) is rude.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je veux bien venir, à condition qu'on ___ en train."
questions.explanation: "À condition que" takes the subjunctive (lesson 08): "qu'on parte" (from "ils partent").

questions.stem: Tom arrives an hour late again. His friend says: "Tu exagères !" What does she mean?
questions.explanation: "Exagérer" means "to exaggerate" and also "to go too far". Here she is criticising his lateness.

questions.stem: "Le cinéma ou le restaurant ? — Ça m'est égal." What does the speaker mean?
questions.explanation: "Ça m'est égal" = it's all the same to me, I don't mind which. Said flatly it can sound as if you don't care, so watch your tone.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ça te dérange ___ j'ouvre la fenêtre ?"
questions.explanation: "Ça te dérange si" + indicative: "si j'ouvre". ("Ça te dérange que j'ouvre", with the subjunctive, also exists; "de", "à" and "pour" don't work before a clause.)

questions.stem: Complete with "céder" in the present: "Nous ne ___ pas."
questions.explanation: "Céder" is like "préférer": "è" only when the next syllable has a silent -e (je cède, ils cèdent); "nous cédons" keeps "é".

questions.stem: Which sentence reformulates what the other person said?
choices: En tout cas, il faut décider.
Si je comprends bien, tu préfères partir en juin ?
questions.explanation: "Si je comprends bien, …" says the other person's idea again to check it: that is reformulation. The others interrupt, accept, or move the discussion on.

questions.stem: In the dialogue about the long weekend, why does Hugo object to a house by the sea?
choices: He has to work in May.
questions.explanation: Hugo says "Ce qui compte pour moi, c'est le prix" and "il faut tenir compte du budget de chacun". He has "rien contre la mer".

questions.stem: Which expression means "to take into account"?
questions.explanation: "Tenir compte de" = to take into account. "Rendre compte de" = to report on, "se rendre compte" = to realise, "compter sur" = to count on.

questions.stem: Which sentences are polite ways to disagree? Select all that apply.
choices: Je ne serais pas tout à fait d'accord.
Je verrais plutôt les choses autrement.
questions.explanation: Partial agreement ("Tu n'as pas tort, mais …") and the conditionnel ("Je ne serais pas …", "Je verrais plutôt …") soften disagreement. "Tais-toi" and "C'est nul" are rude.

questions.stem: Put this negotiation in order.
choices: Léa : Et si on louait une maison à la mer ?
Hugo : C'est trop cher pour moi.
Léa : D'accord, oublions la maison. Et un petit appartement ?
Hugo : Un appartement, je veux bien, à condition qu'il ne soit pas trop cher.
questions.explanation: A proposal, an objection, a concession that answers the objection (giving up the house and offering a flat), a condition attached to the flat, and the close.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Arrête de me couper la ___ !"
questions.explanation: "Couper la parole à quelqu'un" = to cut someone off. "La parole" is the turn to speak.

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Le compromis" = compromise, "le désaccord" = disagreement, "céder" = to give in, "nuancer" = to qualify an opinion. "To negotiate" is "négocier".

questions.stem: What is each numbered speaker doing?

image.alt: Four panels, each with a person and a speech bubble, and an empty numbered box under the bubble. 1: Pardon de te couper, mais … 2: Tu peux préciser ? 3: Tu n'as pas tort, mais … 4: Coupons la poire en deux !

questions.explanation: 1 "Pardon de te couper, mais …" interrupts politely; 2 "Tu peux préciser ?" asks for clarification; 3 "Tu n'as pas tort, mais …" concedes a point before answering; 4 "Coupons la poire en deux !" proposes a compromise. Nobody is closing the discussion ("Alors, c'est décidé") or reformulating ("Si je comprends bien …").

questions.stem: Which describes a learner at CEFR level B1?
choices: They can only use a few simple set phrases.
They understand virtually everything they hear or read.
They can describe experiences and plans and briefly give reasons for their opinions.
They write complex academic texts in their field.
questions.explanation: B1, the first "independent user" level, is about connected speech and writing on familiar topics, with reasons and explanations. Set phrases only is A1; understanding virtually everything is C2; complex texts in your field are B2–C1.

questions.stem: How do you pass the DELF B1?
choices: 50/100 overall, and at least 5/25 in every part
50/100 overall, whatever the marks in each part
questions.explanation: You need 50 points out of 100 and at least 5 out of 25 in each of the four parts. A mark below 5 in any part is éliminatoire, even with 50 or more in total.

questions.stem: In the listening paper, how many times do you hear each recording?
choices: as many times as you like
questions.explanation: Each of the three recordings is heard twice: use the first time to answer what you can and the second to check.

questions.stem: Which part of the DELF B1 comes with 10 minutes of preparation?
choices: the third part of the speaking test
questions.explanation: Only the third part of the speaking test (a point of view from a short document) is prepared, for 10 minutes. The guided interview and the role play are not prepared.

questions.stem: What does "éliminatoire" mean in "Une note inférieure à 5 sur 25 est éliminatoire"?
choices: It is removed from the total.
It is the best possible mark.
It makes you fail the whole exam.
You must retake that part the next day.
questions.explanation: An "éliminatoire" mark fails you, whatever your total.

questions.stem: What is "la problématique" of a topic?
questions.explanation: "La problématique" is the key question your text has to answer, for example "Travailler moins de jours, est-ce travailler mieux ?" A problem is "un problème".

questions.stem: Complete: "Voici les points ___." (main)
questions.explanation: "Principal" has the masculine plural "principaux" (like "normal → normaux"). "Principales" is feminine and "points" is masculine.

questions.stem: Complete with "se préparer": "Il faut que tu te ___ sérieusement."
questions.explanation: "Il faut que" takes the subjunctive; for "tu" it is "que tu te prépares" (the same as the present here), with the -s of the tu form.

questions.stem: Which meaning of "essai" is used in "J'ai réussi au premier essai"?
questions.explanation: "L'essai" is an essay and also an attempt or try: "au premier essai" = at the first attempt.

questions.stem: Which strategy for multiple-choice listening questions does the lesson recommend?
choices: Read the questions and options before the recording starts.
Choose the option that repeats the most words from the recording.
Leave a question blank when you are not sure.
questions.explanation: Reading the questions first tells you what to listen for. Wrong options often repeat words from the document, and preparation guides say a blank earns nothing while a wrong answer costs nothing.

questions.stem: In the text "Apprendre une langue après quarante ans", what advantage do adults have?
choices: They are never afraid of making mistakes.
They know why they are learning.
questions.explanation: "Surtout, ils savent pourquoi ils apprennent." The better accent and the lack of fear are the children's advantages; the text never says adults learn faster.

questions.stem: In the same text, what helped Marc most?
questions.explanation: Marc says: "Ce qui m'a aidé, c'est de pratiquer un peu tous les jours plutôt que beaucoup une fois par semaine." It's his daughter who lives in Milan, and he now watches films without subtitles.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si j'avais su, je ___ venu."
questions.explanation: Si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé (lesson 11): "je serais venu". "Venir" takes être.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Bien que je sois fatigué, je continue.
Bien que je suis fatigué, je continue.
Bien que je serais fatigué, je continue.
questions.explanation: In standard French "bien que" takes the subjunctive, even when the subject is the same in both halves: "bien que je sois".

questions.stem: Which statements about the DELF B1 are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Each of the four parts is marked out of 25.
The writing paper asks for one text of at least about 160 words.
The speaking test lasts about an hour.
You need at least 5/25 in each part.
The three written parts are taken on three different days.
questions.explanation: Each part is marked out of 25; the writing paper asks for one text of at least about 160 words; and you need at least 5/25 in each part. The speaking test lasts about 15 minutes, and the three written parts are taken together in one sitting.

questions.stem: Type the verb in the subjunctive: "Il faut que tu ___ ta réponse." (justifier)
questions.explanation: "Il faut que" + subjunctive: from "ils justifient", "que tu justifies".

questions.stem: Put the steps of the writing paper in order.
choices: Read the task and find the problématique
Plan: your position, two or three arguments, an example for each
questions.explanation: Find the question first, then plan, then write, and keep the last minutes for rereading with the checklist of lesson 22.

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "L'orthographe" = spelling, "la ponctuation" = punctuation, "la conjugaison" = conjugation, "la cohérence" = coherence, "l'aisance" = ease, fluency. "Vocabulary" is "le vocabulaire".

questions.stem: Name the four parts of the DELF B1.

image.alt: The DELF B1 overview chart with the names of the four parts replaced by numbered empty boxes. 1: about 25 min, 3 recordings, each heard twice. 2: 45 min, short texts and two longer texts. 3: 45 min, one text, at least about 160 words. 4, in the speaking test box: about 15 min, 3 parts, 10 min preparation for part 3 only. Each part is worth 25 points.

questions.explanation: 1 listening (compréhension de l'oral: recordings heard twice), 2 reading (compréhension des écrits), 3 writing (production écrite: one text of at least about 160 words), 4 speaking (production et interaction orales, about 15 minutes). The "monologue suivi" is a part of the A2 speaking test, and the DELF has no translation paper.

questions.stem: In a dialectical plan, what does the antithèse do?
choices: It gives your own final answer.
It presents the opposite answer fairly.
questions.explanation: Part 2, the antithèse, gives the other side its full turn, as fairly as the thèse. Your final answer is the synthèse.

questions.stem: What makes a good synthèse?
choices: It answers the question more precisely, often with conditions.
It repeats the thèse in other words.
It says both sides are equally right.
questions.explanation: A synthèse goes beyond both sides: "yes, if …", "only when …". Repeating the thèse or saying "both are right" is the most common weakness.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Ce livre, il s'agit d'une famille.
Il s'agit ce livre d'une famille.
Dans ce livre, il s'agit d'une famille.
questions.explanation: "Il s'agit de" is impersonal: its subject is always "il". Say "Dans ce livre, il s'agit de …" or "Ce livre parle de …".

questions.stem: What is "l'ouverture" at the end of an essay?
choices: a wider question the essay leads to
questions.explanation: The ouverture opens onto a bigger, related question without answering it. A new argument belongs in the body.

questions.stem: What does "Or" do in "On dit que les écrans isolent les jeunes. Or, la plupart de leurs échanges se font avec des amis."?
choices: It brings in a fact that changes the reasoning.
questions.explanation: "Or" (the conjunction) is a formal connector that introduces a fact that undermines or changes the argument: "but, yet, now". "L'or" is gold and "or" in English is "ou".

questions.stem: Which expression is formal and introduces a fact you can't deny?
questions.explanation: "Force est de constater que" = one has to admit that; it belongs to formal writing. The others are neutral or spoken.

questions.stem: Complete: "Force est de constater que le projet ___ échoué."
questions.explanation: "Force est de constater que" introduces an undeniable fact, so it takes the indicative: "a échoué".

questions.stem: What does "raisonner" mean?
questions.explanation: "Raisonner" = to reason (le raisonnement = reasoning). "Résonner", with an é, is to resonate or echo.

questions.stem: In a refutation, what comes after "Certains affirment que …"?
choices: what is true in that view, then why it fails
questions.explanation: Refutation has three steps: state the other view fairly, grant what is true in it ("Il est vrai que …"), then show where it fails ("Or …, cet argument ne tient pas").

questions.stem: Which essay question suits a dialectical plan best?
choices: Écrivez une lettre pour réserver une chambre.
questions.explanation: A yes-or-no question about a debatable issue can be answered "yes", then "no", then "yes, if …". A description, a story or a booking letter has no two sides to weigh.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a dialectical essay in order.
choices: La synthèse: a more precise answer
questions.explanation: Introduction (with the question), thèse, antithèse, synthèse, conclusion (with an ouverture).

questions.stem: Match each expression with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "À première vue" = at first sight, "en définitive" = all things considered, "en somme" = in short (close to "bref"), "il s'agit de" = it's a matter of. "In other words" is "autrement dit".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the dialectical plan.

image.alt: Two essay plans side by side. Left, the B1 plan: introduction, your position; argument 1 with an example; argument 2 with an example; the other side, briefly, certes … mais; conclusion, your position again. Right, the dialectical plan (B2): introduction, the question; then three boxes with empty numbered slots: 1 the arguments for, 2 the arguments against, 3 a more careful answer; and a conclusion with a fourth empty slot: plus a wider question.

questions.explanation: 1 the thèse (the arguments for), 2 the antithèse (the arguments against), 3 the synthèse (a more careful answer), 4 the ouverture (the wider question in the conclusion). "La réfutation" answers one argument; "la problématique" is the question asked in the introduction.

questions.stem: Type the noun made from "réfuter": "la ___"
questions.explanation: "Réfuter → la réfutation", like "illustrer → l'illustration".

questions.stem: Which sentences answer an opposing argument (refutation)? Select all that apply.
choices: Certains affirment que les écrans isolent les jeunes. Or, la plupart de leurs échanges se font avec des amis.
On pourrait objecter que le télétravail isole ; cet argument ne tient pas, car les équipes se retrouvent chaque semaine.
Le télétravail est un sujet important.
questions.explanation: The first two state the other view and then show why it fails ("Or, …", "cet argument ne tient pas, car …"). The last two only give an opinion or a fact; they answer nobody.

questions.stem: In the DELF B1 speaking test, which part do you prepare?
questions.explanation: Only part 3 (a point of view from a short document) is prepared, for 10 minutes. The guided interview and the role play are not prepared.

questions.stem: What does "avoir le trac" mean?
choices: to be nervous before speaking or performing
to lose your train of thought
questions.explanation: "Le trac" is stage fright; "avoir le trac" = to be nervous before an oral, a concert or a talk.

questions.stem: Complete: "Avant un oral, j'___ toujours le trac."
questions.explanation: It's "avoir le trac": "j'ai le trac", not "je suis le trac".

questions.stem: During the 10 minutes of preparation, what should you write?
choices: key words and a short plan
a list of words to learn by heart
questions.explanation: Key words and a plan help you speak; full sentences make you read aloud, and examiners want to hear you speak.

questions.stem: You lose your thread in the middle of your talk. Which phrase helps you pick up again?
questions.explanation: "Reprendre" = to resume, to pick up again: "Je reprends : …", "Pour reprendre ce que je disais, …".

questions.stem: In "Ton débit est trop rapide", what is "le débit"?
questions.explanation: "Le débit" is how fast you speak. Nerves make it faster; a calm "débit" is easier to follow.

questions.stem: In the model point of view about shared gardens, what is the candidate's position?
choices: Against, because few people take part
In favour, but only for children
In favour, provided the gardens stay open to the whole neighbourhood
questions.explanation: "Pour moi, les jardins partagés sont une bonne idée, à condition qu'ils restent ouverts à tout le quartier." The candidate concedes that it's often the same people, but answers it.

questions.stem: In the model role play about the dog, how does the candidate show she has understood her flatmate?
choices: She reformulates: « Si je comprends bien, … »
questions.explanation: "Si je comprends bien, il resterait seul presque toute la journée ?" checks her understanding before she objects: that is reformulation.

questions.stem: Which advice about nerves does the lesson give?
choices: Speak as fast as you can to finish sooner.
Slow down and look at the examiner.
questions.explanation: A slower "débit", clear "articulation" and eye contact ("le regard") make you easier to follow and calmer.

questions.stem: Complete: "Allez, je me ___ !"
questions.explanation: "Se lancer" in the present: "je me lance" (here goes!). "Lances" is the tu form.

questions.stem: Which are good ways to keep going when you can't find a word? Select all that apply.
choices: Describe it: « C'est un truc qui sert à … »
Use a more general word, such as « la chose » or « l'outil »
Stop and translate it in your head
Stay silent until it comes back
questions.explanation: Describe it ("C'est un truc qui sert à …") or use a more general word. Stopping to translate in your head, or waiting in silence, breaks the conversation.

questions.stem: Put these steps of the 10-minute preparation in order.
choices: Write the problématique as a question
Choose your position and two arguments with examples
Note an opening and a closing sentence
questions.explanation: Read the document, turn its topic into a question, choose your position and arguments, then prepare your first and last sentences.

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
choices: to pick up on a point
questions.explanation: "Le regard" = look, eye contact; "articuler" = to speak clearly; "rebondir" = to pick up on a point; "improviser" = to improvise. "To pause" is "faire une pause".

questions.stem: Type the passé composé of "reprendre": "J'___ mon explication après la pause."
questions.explanation: "Reprendre" is like "prendre": "j'ai repris".

cards.front: La Parure: author, first publication, collection
cards.back: Guy de Maupassant (1850–1893). Le Gaulois, 17 February 1884; then Contes du jour et de la nuit (1885). Free to read on Project Gutenberg (eBook 14790).

Mathilde borrows a diamond necklace for a ball and loses it. The Loisels buy a replacement for 36,000 francs and spend ten years in poverty paying for it. Then she learns that the first necklace was fake, worth 500 francs at most.
Short, few characters, one main event, often a twist ending: la chute. Maupassant wrote about three hundred.
Ordinary Paris people, exact sums of money (400, 18,000, 36,000, 500 francs), ten years of hard work, and a narrator who lets the facts speak.
je parlai, tu parlas, il parla, nous parlâmes, vous parlâtes, ils parlèrent. -ger: il mangea; -cer: il commença.
finis, finis, finit, finîmes, finîtes, finirent (prendre: prit, faire: fit, voir: vit). voulus, voulus, voulut, voulûmes, voulûtes, voulurent (être: fut, avoir: eut, connaître: connut, vivre: vécut).
je vins, tu vins, il vint, nous vînmes, vous vîntes, ils vinrent (tenir: tint, tinrent).
Written narration: passé simple for events + imparfait for background. Speech, dialogue and your own writing: passé composé. Ils vécurent dans la misère = ils ont vécu dans la misère.

cards.front: qu'il fût, qu'il eût, qu'il parlât
cards.back: Imperfect subjunctive (literary): from the tu passé simple minus -s + -sse…: today qu'il soit, qu'il ait, qu'il parle. Recognise only. Without the circumflex, il fut is the passé simple.
Literary pluperfect subjunctive used for the conditionnel passé: = elle aurait aimé briller (she would have liked to shine). A B2 point: recognise only.
About 396 million in 2025 (348 million with the older method); nearly 65 % in Africa; the fourth most spoken language in the world. An estimate.
90 states and governments: 53 full members, 5 associate members, 32 observers. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger announced their withdrawal in March 2025. Francophonie day: 20 March.
Belgium: French, Dutch, German. Switzerland: German, French, Italian, Romansh. Canada: English and French (French alone in Québec; co-official in New Brunswick).
A form of a language used in one region or group, with its own accent, words and some grammar, still understood by other speakers. Québec, Belgian, Swiss, African and France French are all varieties.

A language born from contact between speakers of different languages; most words from one language (French, for Haiti, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Réunion), but its own grammar. Haitian Creole is official in Haiti, with French.
le dépanneur = corner shop (in France, a breakdown mechanic); magasiner = to go shopping; le chum = friend, boyfriend (informal), ma blonde = my girlfriend.
Belgium: le kot = student room; la drache = downpour (also northern France); le GSM = mobile phone. Switzerland: le natel = mobile phone. Both: septante, nonante.
A word or expression used in one region only: septante, le dépanneur, le natel. Recognise them; use France's words unless you live there.
Louis the German and Charles the Bald swear an alliance; Louis swears in the Romance language of Charles's soldiers. Copied by Nithard: the first written trace of the language that became French.
French of roughly the 9th to the 14th century: two noun cases, many regional forms. North: langue d'oïl (oïl = yes); south: langue d'oc.
Gaulish: le chêne, le mouton, la ruche, l'alouette. Frankish: la guerre, le jardin, bleu, blanc, gris, and the aspirated h (la honte, haïr).
One Latin word, two French words: passed down (popular) and borrowed later from written Latin (learned): hôtel / hôpital, frêle / fragile, poison / potion.
forêt (forest), fête (feast), hôpital (hospital), île (isle), côte (coast): put the s back to find the English cognate.
1539: ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts, French for legal and administrative documents. 1635: Richelieu founds the Académie française. 1694: its first dictionary.
Optional; both spellings correct. No circumflex on i/u (paraitre, le cout; but sûr, mûr, dû and verb endings such as nous fûmes keep it), hyphens in numbers (vingt-et-un), ognon, évènement.
Québec from the late 1970s; France guidance 1986 and 1998; accepted by the Académie française in 2019: la professeure, l'autrice, la cheffe.

cards.front: Words that went to English and came back
cards.back: tenez → tennis, bougette → budget, tonnelle → tunnel (as etymological dictionaries trace them).
Louis Braille (1809–1852), blind from childhood, published a system of up to six raised dots per sign: 63 usable patterns. He built on Charles Barbier's night writing.
6 July 1885: Joseph Meister, nine, bitten by a rabid dog, is treated with Pasteur's vaccine and survives. The Institut Pasteur opens in 1888.
First launch on 24 December 1979 from Kourou, French Guiana: a European launcher (un lanceur) built so that Europe could put its own satellites into orbit.
First commercial service 27 September 1981, Paris–Lyon. Rail speed record 574.8 km/h (574,8 km/h in French), 3 April 2007, on the high-speed line to eastern France.
Videotex terminal launched in 1982 and given free to telephone subscribers (directory, train tickets, 3615 services); closed on 30 June 2012.
fermer → la fermeture, lancer → le lancement, mettre en service → la mise en service, découvrir → la découverte. La fermeture du Minitel (2012).
un programme spatial, l'industrie spatiale, des programmes spatiaux. Ferroviaire has one form: le réseau ferroviaire, une ligne ferroviaire.
Title (often with a colon), an opening question, facts with dates, two points of view (certains pensent que … d'autres répondent que …), a conclusion that opens a wider question.
un brevet = a patent (déposer un brevet); un prototype = the first working model; une innovation = something new that is actually used (innover).

cards.front: Imparfait or passé composé: the order of questions
cards.back: 1. A habit? → imparfait. 2. A stated length or number (pendant six heures, trois fois)? → passé composé. 3. Moves the story on, or a reaction? → passé composé. Otherwise it is the scene → imparfait.

cards.front: nous avons marché six heures / chaque matin, nous marchions six heures
cards.back: One walk with a stated length: passé composé. The same walk as a habit: imparfait.
I was afraid (a state) / I got scared (a reaction at that moment)
I knew / I found out
I knew (a person, a place) / I met (for the first time)
I could, I was able to / I managed to
I wanted / I tried to, I decided to (je n'ai pas voulu = I refused)
I was supposed to / I had to (and did); il a dû se perdre = he must have got lost

cards.front: il y avait / il y a eu
cards.back: there was (a situation) / there was (something happened): il y a eu un orage

cards.front: Je suis sorti / J'ai sorti les valises
cards.back: Sortir, monter, descendre, rentrer, passer, retourner take avoir with a direct object: I went out / I took the cases out.
Only with a direct object placed before the verb: La tente ? Je l'ai montée. Les photos que j'ai prises.
No agreement: se rendre compte is an exception (se is not the direct object).

cards.front: un beau jour, ce jour-là, sur le coup, aussitôt, brusquement
cards.back: one fine day, that day, at first (in the moment), immediately, abruptly: markers that usually introduce events (passé composé)
Imparfait of avoir or être + past participle: j'avais fini, elle était partie, ils s'étaient trompés.
Exactly as in the passé composé: être for movement verbs and pronominal verbs (agree with the subject); avoir agrees with a direct object before it.
Around the auxiliary: Je ne l'avais pas vu. Elle n'était jamais venue.
1. Before another past action (le film avait commencé). 2. Explaining a past situation (on lui avait menti). 3. What had or hadn't happened before the story (elle n'avait jamais vu la mer).

cards.front: Quand je suis arrivé, il est parti / il était parti
cards.back: He left when I arrived / he had already left before I arrived

cards.front: "I had been waiting for an hour when …"
cards.back: J'attendais depuis une heure quand … (imparfait + depuis, not the plus-que-parfait)
the day before (in a story; from today: hier) / before, earlier (formal; in speech avant)
chance, by chance; aspirated h: le hasard, never l'hasard
avoir: il a disparu, mon vélo avait disparu
to lie to someone (je mens, nous mentons; il m'a menti); le mensonge = a lie
après avoir mangé, après être arrivé(e)(s), après s'être levé(e)(s): same subject only; same auxiliary and agreement as the passé composé
avant de + plain infinitive (avant de partir); après + past infinitive (après être parti)

cards.front: After + verb with a different subject
cards.back: après que + indicative: Après que son frère est parti, elle a repris l'atelier.
Indicative in careful French (après qu'il est parti); the subjunctive (après qu'il soit parti) is common, especially in speech.

cards.front: dès que, aussitôt que, une fois que
cards.back: as soon as, as soon as (more written), once: + indicative

cards.front: au moment où, tant que, chaque fois que
cards.back: (just) when / just as, as long as, every time: + indicative

cards.front: Time clauses in the past: one event or a habit?
cards.back: One event: passé composé (Dès qu'il est arrivé, on a commencé). A habit: imparfait, often with a plus-que-parfait in the clause (Dès qu'il avait fini, il sortait).
le lendemain, la veille; aujourd'hui → ce jour-là
l'année précédente / l'année suivante

cards.front: il y a deux jours / dans deux jours → ? (in a story)
cards.back: deux jours plus tôt (avant) / deux jours plus tard (après)
Still masculine: Marie Curie était un génie.

cards.front: How is the present participle made?
cards.back: nous present minus -ons + -ant: conduisons → conduisant, finissons → finissant, mangeons → mangeant
être → étant, avoir → ayant, savoir → sachant
at the same time (en conduisant), how (on apprend en pratiquant), if (en partant tôt, tu éviteras …), when (en arrivant au rond-point, …)
Always the subject of the main verb. Not: En traversant, une voiture m'a renversé. Say: Pendant que je traversais, une voiture m'a renversé.
at the same time, often with a contrast: Il roulait vite tout en sachant que c'était dangereux (even though he knew).
Mostly written: instead of qui + verb (les passagers voyageant à l'arrière) or for a cause (Étant fatiguée, elle s'est arrêtée). Never agrees.
Participle = action, invariable, often with a complement (des enfants obéissant à leurs parents). Adjective = quality, agrees, can take très (des enfants obéissants).
present participle / verbal adjective (un trajet fatigant, l'année précédente)
J'aime conduire. Arrête de parler. (infinitives: not every -ing is a gérondif)
the car park (the place) / parking (the act): Stationnement interdit = No parking
Motorway 130 km/h (110 in the rain); two-way roads outside towns usually 80 km/h (90 in some départements); towns 50 km/h, sometimes 30
Maria Skłodowska, born 7 November 1867 in Warsaw (then in the Russian Empire); in Paris from late 1891
1903 Physics, shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel (the first woman laureate); 1911 Chemistry, alone
Announced by the Curies in 1898 (July and December); polonium was named after Poland. Marie coined the word radioactivité.
Pierre died on 19 April 1906 (street accident); she became the first woman to teach at the Sorbonne. She died on 4 July 1934 in Passy (Haute-Savoie).
20 April 1995: her ashes and Pierre's were moved there; the first woman honoured there for her own merits
The present used for past events, common in French history and biographies: En 1891, elle part pour Paris.

cards.front: Historic present: what happens to the other tenses?
cards.back: Events: present (elle part). Earlier past: passé composé (que Becquerel a découverts). Later events: futur (elle recevra un second prix Nobel).

cards.front: One rule for the historic present
cards.back: Choose a past narration or the historic present for a passage and keep it: don't switch at random.
widow / widower: elle est restée veuve
to pay tribute to someone: la France leur a rendu hommage
ayant + participle (ayant marché), étant + participle for être verbs (étant arrivé(e)s): having done
A past participle alone opening the sentence: it belongs to the subject (nous) and agrees with it. Written style for "quand nous sommes arrivés".
A participle clause with its own subject (le brouillard): formal written style, "the fog having lifted".
une fois + noun + participle: once the glacier had been rounded
Not: Arrivés au sommet, le brouillard est tombé (the fog arrived?). Say: Quand nous sommes arrivés au sommet, le brouillard est tombé.
a time phrase (La veille, …), a marker (Brusquement, …), a perfect participle, a participle clause, an adjective (Épuisés, …), a place (Devant nous, …)
fog (thick) / mist (light)
dawn / dusk

cards.front: le col, le refuge, la falaise, le glacier
cards.back: mountain pass, mountain hut, cliff, glacier
Indicative: facts, what you present as real (Je sais que tu viens). Subjunctive: what is needed, wanted, felt or doubted, almost always after que (Il faut que tu viennes).
The ils present without -ent + -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent: ils parlent → que je parle; ils finissent → que je finisse; ils attendent → que j'attende.
They look like the imparfait: que nous venions, que vous preniez, que nous étudiions (double i), que nous voyions.
venir: vienne / venions; prendre: prenne / prenions; boire: boive / buvions; devoir: doive / devions; recevoir: reçoive / recevions; voir: voie / voyions; appeler: appelle / appelions.
être sois, avoir aie, aller aille, faire fasse, pouvoir puisse, savoir sache, vouloir veuille. Also qu'il faille, qu'il pleuve.

cards.front: être and avoir in the subjunctive
cards.back: sois, sois, soit, soyons, soyez, soient; aie, aies, ait, ayons, ayez, aient (no i in nous / vous).
que j'aille, que tu ailles, qu'il aille, qu'ils aillent, but que nous allions, que vous alliez; que je veuille … but que nous voulions, que vous vouliez.
il faut que, il est nécessaire / important / essentiel / indispensable que, il vaut mieux que, il suffit que.

cards.front: il faut + infinitive or il faut que?
cards.back: General rule: Il faut réserver à l'avance. A particular person: Il faut que tu réserves à l'avance.

cards.front: must not or don't have to?
cards.back: Il ne faut pas que tu viennes = you mustn't come. Il n'est pas nécessaire que tu viennes / Tu n'es pas obligé de venir = you don't have to come.
vouloir, aimer (bien), souhaiter, désirer, préférer, exiger, demander, accepter, refuser que, tenir à ce que, insister pour que + subjunctive: Je veux que tu ranges ta chambre.
être content / triste / désolé / surpris / déçu / fier que, avoir peur que, craindre que, regretter que, c'est dommage que, ça m'étonne que: Je suis content que tu sois là.
Je veux partir (not que je parte). Feelings take de: Je suis content de te voir; j'ai peur d'être en retard.

cards.front: demander / interdire / permettre à quelqu'un de
cards.back: The everyday pattern: Je te demande de ranger ta chambre. Mes parents m'interdisent de sortir. But: autoriser quelqu'un à faire.
Indicative in the affirmative, often the futur: J'espère que tu viendras. Compare souhaiter que + subjunctive: Je souhaite que tu viennes.
J'ai peur qu'il ne pleuve = I'm afraid it will rain. Not negative, optional, careful French. A real negative needs pas.
disappointed, offended (hurt pride), embarrassed, relieved, moved. All + que + subjunctive.
je crains, nous craignons, ils craignent; j'ai craint; que je craigne. More formal than avoir peur.
Certain / probable → indicative (je suis sûr que, il est probable que, je pense que). Possible / doubtful → subjunctive (il est possible que, il se peut que, je doute que).
Je pense / crois / trouve que + indicative. Je ne pense / crois / trouve pas que + subjunctive (Je ne pense pas que ce soit vrai).
Indicative: Il est probable qu'il viendra. But il est peu probable / improbable que + subjunctive.

cards.front: il se peut que / peut-être que
cards.back: Both mean "maybe". Il se peut qu'il pleuve (subjunctive); peut-être qu'il pleuvra (indicative).

cards.front: il semble que / il me semble que / il paraît que
cards.back: Il semble que + usually subjunctive (it seems). Il me semble que + indicative (I think). Il paraît que + indicative (apparently, people say).
probably (not "without doubt", which is sans aucun doute): Il a sans doute raison.
je parais, il paraît, nous paraissons; j'ai paru. Also "to come out" (a book). 1990: paraitre, il parait.
Penses-tu qu'il ait raison ? (subjunctive possible) or … qu'il a raison ? With est-ce que or intonation, the indicative is usual.
pour que, afin que, avant que, jusqu'à ce que, sans que, à condition que, pourvu que, à moins que, bien que, quoique.
parce que, pendant que, alors que, dès que, après que (careful French), même si.
pour / afin de, avant de, sans, à condition de, à moins de + infinitive: Je travaille pour gagner ma vie. No everyday partner for bien que, quoique, jusqu'à ce que, pourvu que.
provided that (Tu peux venir, pourvu que tu sois à l'heure) or, alone, a wish: Pourvu qu'il fasse beau ! = Let's hope it's nice!
Careful French may add a ne explétif: avant qu'il ne soit trop tard; à moins qu'il ne pleuve. Not negative.
quoique (one word) = although = bien que. quoi que (two words) = whatever. Both + subjunctive.
Like tenir: je soutiens, nous soutenons, ils soutiennent; j'ai soutenu; je soutiendrai; que je soutienne.
le / la bénévole (volunteer), l'association (charity), la collecte (collection), le don (donation), s'engager (to get involved), le soutien (support).

cards.front: Subjonctif passé: how to form it
cards.back: avoir / être in the subjunctive + past participle: que j'aie fini, qu'elle soit partie, qu'ils se soient trompés.
Présent: same time or later than the main verb (Je suis content que tu viennes). Passé: already finished (Je suis content que tu sois venu).

cards.front: Subjonctif passé with a future deadline
cards.back: Il faut que tu aies fini avant 18 heures. Attends jusqu'à ce que j'aie terminé.
As in the passé composé: être → agreement with the subject (que ma sœur soit arrivée); avoir → with a direct object placed before.
Toutes mes félicitations ! Je suis si heureux / fier que tu aies réussi. Nous sommes ravis que votre fille soit née.
Je te présente mes sincères condoléances. J'ai appris avec beaucoup de peine le décès de … Je compatis à ta peine. Je pense fort à toi.
Formal: le décès de ton père; il est décédé le 3 mars. Everyday: la mort, il est mort.
An announcement card: faire-part de naissance, de mariage, de décès. Plural les faire-part. Nous avons la tristesse de vous faire part du décès de …

cards.front: la peine, le chagrin, le deuil, le réconfort
cards.back: sorrow (also trouble, effort), grief, mourning (être en deuil), comfort (consolation; physical comfort is le confort).
que + subjunctive in a main clause, for a third person: Qu'il entre ! Que personne ne bouge ! Que le meilleur gagne !
The old subjunctive of vivre: Vive la mariée ! Before a plural, usually invariable: Vive les vacances ! (vivent also accepted).
Fine! So be it! (often said [swat]). soit … soit = either … or; soit = that is (trois jours, soit 72 heures).
Ainsi soit-il (amen), Sauve qui peut ! (every man for himself), coûte que coûte (at all costs), advienne que pourra (come what may).

cards.front: quoi que, où que, qui que
cards.back: whatever, wherever, whoever + subjunctive: Quoi que tu fasses … Où que tu ailles … Qui que vous soyez …
quel agrees with the noun, soit with its number: quel que soit le prix, quelle que soit la raison, quels que soient les risques, quelles que soient tes idées.

cards.front: qui que ce soit / quoi que ce soit
cards.back: anyone at all / anything at all: Ne le dis à qui que ce soit. Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, appelle-moi.

cards.front: quoique or quoi que: the test
cards.back: Replace it with bien que. If it works → quoique (although). If it means "whatever" → quoi que.
1 si + present → present / futur / imperative (real). 2 si + imparfait → conditionnel présent (unreal now, unlikely). 3 si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé (unreal past).

cards.front: The golden rule after si (= if)
cards.back: Never the futur, never the conditionnel: si j'avais (not si j'aurais), s'il fait beau (not s'il fera). The conditionnel goes in the other half.
In an indirect question si means "whether" and takes any tense: Je me demande si je serais heureux à la campagne. Je ne sais pas s'il viendra.

cards.front: si je gagne / si je gagnais
cards.back: Both are correct. Type 1 (gagne … partirai): it could happen. Type 2 (gagnais … partirais): it probably won't, but imagine. What is plainly untrue now is always type 2.
A past habit, not an unreal condition: S'il pleuvait, on restait à la maison (whenever it rained).
Even if: the same tenses as si, always the indicative. Même s'il pleut, on sortira. Même si j'étais riche, je travaillerais.
cards.topic: Même si, sinon, au cas où

cards.back: In case: + conditionnel. Prends un parapluie au cas où il pleuvrait. Alone: Prends un pull, au cas où (just in case).
cards.topic: Même si, sinon, au cas où

cards.back: Otherwise, or else (one word): Pars maintenant, sinon tu vas rater ton train. After a fact, + conditionnel: Heureusement que j'ai une voiture, sinon je serais coincé.
cards.topic: Même si, sinon, au cas où

cards.front: niveau de vie, qualité de vie, mode de vie, coût de la vie
cards.back: Standard of living (what you can afford); quality of life (how good life feels); lifestyle; cost of living.
Je suppose que + indicative = I assume. Supposons que + subjunctive sets up a hypothesis: Supposons que tu aies raison.
cards.topic: Même si, sinon, au cas où

cards.front: Conditionnel passé: how to build it
cards.back: Conditionnel of avoir or être + past participle: j'aurais aimé, elle serait venue, nous nous serions trompés. Same auxiliaries and agreement as the passé composé.
j'ai fini (passé composé), j'avais fini (plus-que-parfait), j'aurais fini (conditionnel passé), j'aurai fini (futur antérieur).
I should have / I could have, + a plain infinitive: J'aurais dû partir plus tôt. Tu aurais pu me prévenir !

cards.front: je devrais, j'ai dû, j'aurais dû
cards.back: I should (now); I had to (or I must have); I should have (but didn't).
+ infinitive: it would have been necessary, we should have. Il aurait fallu réserver plus tôt.

Regret (j'aurais aimé), reproach (vous auriez pu appeler), missed chance (on aurait pu gagner), polite past (j'aurais voulu savoir), after si + plus-que-parfait, and unconfirmed news (aurait fait deux blessés).
To accept responsibility for: assumer ses choix. "To assume" (suppose) is supposer.
reprocher quelque chose à quelqu'un: Elle me reproche mon retard. Il me reproche de ne jamais appeler.

cards.front: une bêtise, une gaffe, une maladresse
cards.back: A silly thing; a social blunder, saying the wrong thing (informal); a clumsy act or remark.
si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé: Si j'avais su, je serais venu. Reverse the facts: I didn't know, I didn't come.
si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel présent: Si j'avais pris le train, je serais déjà là.
si + imparfait → conditionnel passé: Si j'étais plus courageux, je l'aurais fait.
+ imparfait: a wish now (Si seulement j'avais le temps !). + plus-que-parfait: a regret (Si seulement je l'avais écouté !).
sans + noun: Sans ton aide, j'aurais abandonné. à ta place: À ta place, j'aurais refusé.

cards.front: le coup de foudre / le coup de chance
cards.back: Love at first sight (pour quelqu'un, pour une ville) / a stroke of luck. Bad luck: la malchance.
croiser quelqu'un = to come across, pass someone; croiser les bras = to fold your arms. To cross a street = traverser.

cards.front: se débrouiller, s'en sortir, se reconvertir
cards.back: To get by, manage; to pull through, cope (je m'en suis sorti); to retrain, change careers.
For a future action, French uses the futur after quand, lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que, une fois que, tant que: Quand tu arriveras, on mangera (English: when you arrive).

cards.front: Futur antérieur: how to build it
cards.back: Futur of avoir or être + past participle: j'aurai fini, elle sera partie, nous nous serons levés.

cards.front: Futur antérieur: what it is for
cards.back: An action finished before another future one (Quand tu auras fini, tu m'appelleras) or by a date (D'ici 2030, on aura construit …).
A guess about the past: he must have forgotten (= il a dû oublier). Recognition only.
j'aurai fini = I will have finished (futur antérieur); j'aurais fini = I would have finished (conditionnel passé). One letter, two meanings.
A habit (whenever): Quand il pleut, je prends le bus. Relaxed speech also says Quand tu arrives, tu m'appelles for a plan; in writing, use the futur.
d'ici + time or date = by, between now and: d'ici 2030, d'ici demain; d'ici là = by then. Also "from here".
To develop, lay out (an area) or fit out (a room); to move in; to move house. Nous aménageons.
Alternate history: u- (no) + chronos (time), like l'utopie. Word coined by Charles Renouvier (1857; book Uchronie, 1876).
Louis Geoffroy, Napoléon et la conquête du monde (1812–1832): Napoléon wins in Russia and conquers the world. Often called the first book built on a point of divergence.
20 March back at the Tuileries; 16 June Ligny; 18 June Waterloo; 22 June second abdication; 15 October Saint Helena. Died 5 May 1821.
Heavy rain the day before soaked the ground, so the attack began late in the morning; Wellington held; Blücher's Prussians arrived in the afternoon, and Grouchy didn't.
Si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé (Si Grouchy était arrivé, Napoléon aurait peut-être gagné) or conditionnel présent for a result today.
Each result becomes the next si clause, in the plus-que-parfait: … aurait attaqué. S'il avait attaqué, …
Facts in the indicative (Napoléon a abdiqué); invented events in the conditionnel (son fils aurait régné), hedged with peut-être, sans doute, aurait pu.
To defeat: il vainc, ils vainquent, participle vaincu. Not drilled; in speech, battre (to beat) is more common.
To reign (il règne, nous régnons), the reign. L'empereur, l'impératrice; le roi, la reine.
Unconfirmed information in the news: Le suspect serait en fuite (reportedly), aurait quitté le pays (is said to have left). Never "would" in translation.
Same time as the indicative: est en fuite → serait en fuite; a quitté → aurait quitté; annoncera demain → annoncerait demain.
To report a claim without vouching for it (sous toutes réserves). The Charter of Munich (1971) asks journalists to publish facts of known origin or with the necessary reservations.
selon, d'après + source; selon nos informations (the paper's own sources); une dépêche de l'AFP; notre correspondant(e); de source sûre (reliable but unnamed).
Alleged (l'auteur présumé); provisional (un bilan provisoire); in all likelihood. All signal caution.
To deny a report officially (un démenti); to lie; to deny doing something (Il nie les faits). Je démens, il dément.
Agence France-Presse: a French news agency, named in 1944; it continued the Agence Havas (1835). Une dépêche = an agency report.
Si j'avais le temps, je lirais … = would (hypothetical). Selon la police, le voleur aurait agi seul = reportedly (news). Look for a source and the context.
Indicative or conditionnel? Which source? Words of caution (présumé, provisoire)? Any démenti? What time was it written?
Instead of de + the antecedent, after verbs, adjectives and nouns with de: le livre dont j'ai besoin, l'œuvre dont il est fier, l'artiste dont le fils est sculpteur.
Normal order, article kept: le peintre dont je connais les œuvres (not dont les œuvres je connais, not dont je connais ses œuvres).
Never: dont isn't a direct object. Les tableaux dont j'ai parlé (but les tableaux que j'ai vus).
la ville d'où il vient (d'où, not dont, for coming from a place).

cards.front: what = ce qui / ce que / ce dont / ce à quoi
cards.back: ce qui + verb (ce qui me plaît); ce que + subject (ce que je veux); ce dont with de verbs (ce dont j'ai besoin); ce à quoi with à verbs (ce à quoi je pense).
tout ce qui (subject) / tout ce que (object): Tout ce que tu vois est à vendre.

cards.front: Mise en relief with ce que … c'est
cards.back: Ce que j'aime, c'est la lumière. Careful French repeats the preposition: Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est de calme; Ce à quoi je pense, c'est à toi.

cards.front: Mise en relief with c'est … qui / que
cards.back: c'est + stressed part + qui (subject) or que (anything else): C'est ce tableau qui m'a touché. C'est à Giverny que Monet a peint.
The verb agrees with the pronoun: c'est moi qui ai choisi, c'est toi qui as raison, c'est nous qui avons payé.
"shay-duh-vr" (silent f); les chefs-d'œuvre.
qui (or lequel): la collègue avec qui je travaille, le client à qui j'ai écrit. After parmi / entre: only lesquels / lesquelles.
lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles (agreeing): le projet sur lequel je travaille, la raison pour laquelle.
auquel, à laquelle, auxquels, auxquelles: le salon auquel nous participons, la question à laquelle j'ai répondu.
After a compound preposition (près de, à côté de, au cours de, au sein de, à l'aide de): duquel, de laquelle, desquels, desquelles. La réunion au cours de laquelle …
de belongs to a verb, adjective or noun → dont (le projet dont je suis responsable); de ends a compound preposition → duquel (le parc près duquel j'habite). Never à côté dont.
Both for a place: le bureau où / dans lequel je travaille. Other place prepositions keep lequel: la table sur laquelle.
When there's no noun: ce à quoi je pense, ce sur quoi il faut insister, quelque chose à quoi je n'avais pas pensé.
Both = a company; la société also = society. Le siège = head office, le service = department, la direction = management, le cadre = executive.
diriger = to run, direct (une équipe; nous dirigeons); gérer = to manage, handle (un budget, le stress; je gère, nous gérons).
être in the tense of the active verb + participle agreeing with the subject: est fabriqué, a été construite, étaient utilisées, sera ouverte, avaient été vendus, doit être réparé.
Never. The second participle agrees: elles ont été vendues.
par for actions (construit par Eiffel); de after feeling and state verbs (aimé de tous, connu de tous, entouré de champs).
No passive with je (indirect object). Use on: On m'a donné un conseil. On m'a dit de partir. On m'a demandé de rester.
1. direct object → subject; 2. être in the same tense + agreeing participle; 3. old subject → par + agent (or drop it). On a fermé l'usine → L'usine a été fermée.
se + verb, third person, for what's usually done: Ça se vend bien. Le vin blanc se boit frais. Ça ne se dit pas. No agent. Passé composé with être: Les billets se sont vendus.

cards.front: Passive or not? Elle est partie.
cards.back: Not a passive: the passé composé of partir. A passive needs a verb with a direct object and can take par + someone: La porte est fermée par le gardien.
fabriquer = to manufacture (Fabriqué en France); produire = to produce (je produis, produit); le fabricant = the manufacturer; la matière première = raw material.
artisanal (artisanaux): made by craftspeople in small workshops; industriel(le): made in factories, on a production line (à la chaîne).

cards.front: Order of two pronouns before the verb
cards.back: me / te / se / nous / vous → le / la / les → lui / leur → y → en. Je te le prête. Je le lui ai rendu. Il y en a.
Together, before the conjugated verb, the auxiliary or the infinitive; ne … pas around it: Je ne le lui ai pas dit. Je vais te le montrer.
verb + direct object + person, en last: Donne-le-moi ! Envoyez-les-leur ! Donnez-m'en ! Negative commands keep statement order: Ne me le donne pas.
me, te, nous, vous never go with lui, leur: Je te présente à lui.
je m'en vais, tu t'en vas, il s'en va, nous nous en allons, vous vous en allez, ils s'en vont; je m'en suis allé(e); Va-t'en ! Allez-vous-en !
Getting it done by someone else: Je fais réparer ma voiture. Pronoun before faire: Je la fais réparer. Je la lui ai fait réparer.

cards.front: Does fait agree before an infinitive?
cards.back: Never: la voiture que j'ai fait réparer; Elle s'est fait couper les cheveux.
Having something done to yourself: Je me suis fait couper les cheveux. Also for mishaps: Il s'est fait voler son portable.
une fuite → le plombier; une serrure → le serrurier; les pneus, la vidange → le mécanicien (au garage); des chaussures → le cordonnier; une veste → le pressing.

cards.front: le devis / la facture / la main-d'œuvre
cards.back: le devis = the quote before the work; la facture = the bill after it; la main-d'œuvre = the cost of the work itself (labour), not the parts.
ne … ni … ni, no pas: Je n'aime ni le thé ni le café. Un, des, du disappear: Je n'ai ni frère ni sœur.
Ni Paul ni Léa ne sont venus (ne kept, verb usually plural). Neither of them: ni l'un ni l'autre.
No article: un café sans sucre, parti sans bagages; sans sucre ni lait.
not a single: Je n'ai pas vu un seul film. Pas un seul client n'est venu.
Formal: Nul ne sait (no one knows), sans nul doute. Informal: Ce film est nul (rubbish), Je suis nul(le) en maths.
hardly, scarcely (written): Il ne mange guère. In speech: Il ne mange presque pas.
n'importe qui (anyone), quoi (anything; nonsense), où (anywhere), quand (any time), comment (any old how); + noun: n'importe quel(le). No ne before the verb.
quiconque (pronoun, formal) = whoever, anyone: mieux que quiconque. quelconque (adjective after the noun) = some … or other, ordinary: pour une raison quelconque.
la tour = tower (la tour Eiffel); le tour = turn, trip around (faire le tour du monument).
la tour, la flèche (spire), la charpente (roof timbers), le vitrail / les vitraux (stained glass), la pierre (stone).
restoring a building or painting (la restauration de Notre-Dame), and the restaurant and catering trade (travailler dans la restauration).
classé monument historique: the highest protection (Notre-Dame, 1862); inscrit: a lighter protection (the Eiffel Tower, since 1964).
begun 1163; restored 1844–1864 (Lassus, Viollet-le-Duc); classée 1862; fire 15 April 2019; reopened 7 December 2024.
built 28 January 1887 – 31 March 1889 for the Exposition universelle of 1889; iron (le fer), about 7,300 tonnes; 300 m then, 330 m with antennas today.

cards.front: Why heritage texts use the passive
cards.back: To keep the building as the subject: La cathédrale a été restaurée … Agents (par …) appear only when the names matter.
They add background without stopping the sentence: Victor Hugo, dont le roman est paru en 1831; des artistes, parmi lesquels Charles Garnier; des usages grâce auxquels la tour a été sauvée.
